definition_zh: 顾客；主顾；客户
definition_en: a person who buys goods or services from a shop or business
core_image: 照着老规矩走进店里买东西的人
scene: 文具店门口排队，店员一边收钱一边笑着说欢迎下次再来。 The shopkeeper greets every customer with a smile.
sceneCN: 这里 customer 是「顾客」（第 1 个义项：从商店购买商品或服务的人）；句意是店主笑着迎接每一位顾客。

derivatives.zh: customer 的同源基础词，义为「习俗；惯例」
由 custom 加 -ary 构成，义为「惯常的」
由 ac- 加 custom 构成，义为「使习惯于」

senses.title: A person who buys things
senses.definition: someone who enters a shop or business and pays for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 进入商店或商家并付钱购买商品或服务的人
senses.example: The first customer of the day bought two notebooks and a pen.
senses.exampleCN: 当天的第一位顾客买了两本笔记本和一支钢笔。
senses.why: Old Latin usage tied buying to settled practice; the person who follows the trade customs became the customer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语的用法把买卖和固定惯例联系在一起，按交易惯例来往的人就成了 customer。

senses.title: A client of a service business
senses.definition: a person who uses a bank, hotel or other service rather than buying goods
senses.definitionCN: 使用银行、酒店等服务的客户，而非购买商品的人
senses.example: The bank serves thousands of customers in our city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家银行服务着本市成千上万的客户。
senses.why: Services also follow fixed routines, so the word spread from shops to banks and hotels.
senses.whyCN: 服务业同样按固定流程办事，这个词便从商店扩展到银行和酒店。

intro.en: Customer grew out of custom, the old word for settled practice.
intro.cn: customer 是从 custom（固定惯例）一词生长出来的。

items.en: consuetudo meant habit or usage, from consuescere, to accustom oneself.
items.cn: 拉丁语 consuetudo 意为习惯、惯例，来自 consuescere（使自己习惯）。

items.en: Old French formed custumier, a person who follows or deals by custom.
items.cn: 古法语形成 custumier，指按惯例行事的人。

items.en: English took customer in the fourteenth century, at first for a person who does business regularly.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 customer，最初指定期做生意的人。

items.en: The sense narrowed to buyers, because steady buyers kept the trade customs.
items.cn: 词义缩小到买家，因为稳定的买家一直遵循交易惯例。

items.en: Today customer names buyers in shops and clients of banks, hotels and phone companies.
items.cn: 如今 customer 指商店的买家和银行、酒店、电话公司的客户。

note.en: These words belong to the custom family or name people who buy and sell.
note.cn: 这些词属于 custom 词族，或指买卖双方。

normal.en: A regular customer comes again and again.

normal.en: customer service is the team that helps buyers.

normal.en: Spelling: customer, not costumer. A costumer makes costumes.
normal.cn: 拼写：customer，别写成 costumer；costumer 是做戏服的人。

normal.en: In a bank you are also a customer, not just in a shop.
normal.cn: 在银行你同样是 customer（客户），不只限于商店。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at the bakery counter, one buyer after another.
abstract.cn: 想象面包店柜台前的队伍，买家一个接一个。

abstract.en: Hear the till ring and the words thank you and come again.
abstract.cn: 听收银机响，听到「谢谢惠顾，欢迎再来」。

abstract.en: Feel the trust that makes someone come back next week.
abstract.cn: 体会让顾客下周还愿意再来的一份信任。

examples.en: There were many customers waiting outside the milk tea shop.
examples.cn: 奶茶店外面有许多顾客在排队。

examples.en: The customer paid by phone and took the receipt.
examples.cn: 顾客用手机付款后拿了小票。

examples.en: Good customer service brings people back to a shop.
examples.cn: 好的客户服务会让人们再次光顾商店。

definition_zh: 自己的；本人的；自己的东西；拥有；承认
definition_en: belonging to oneself, the thing that belongs to oneself, and to have something as property or to admit a fact
core_image: 钥匙串上那把只配你家门的钥匙
scene: 搬家那天，每只纸箱上都写着同一个名字。 After the move she kept her own keys in a small tin box.
sceneCN: 这里 own 是「自己的」（第 1 个义项：属于本人的）；句意为搬完之后，她把自己的钥匙收在一只小铁盒里。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、钥匙、铁盒。

pos.zh: 自己的东西（用在物主词之后）

derivatives.zh: 由 own 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，指拥有某物的人
由 owner 加 -ship 构成，指所有权、产权
home 与 owner 复合而成，指自有住房者

senses.title: Belonging to a particular person
senses.definition: belonging to a particular person rather than to anyone else
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个特定的人，而不是任何别人
senses.example: She keeps her own keys in a small tin box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己的钥匙放在一个小铁盒里。
senses.why: The adjective began as a past participle meaning possessed; it points back at the person who holds the thing, so it always answers the question whose.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最初是表示「被拥有」的过去分词；它回指持有东西的那个人，所以总在回答「谁的」这一问题。

senses.title: The thing that belongs to oneself
senses.definition: used after a possessive word to mean the particular thing or person that belongs to someone
senses.definitionCN: 用在物主词之后，指属于某人的那样东西或那个人
senses.example: He wanted a desk of his own, away from the shared one.
senses.exampleCN: 他想要一张属于自己的桌子，不再和人共用。
senses.why: When the noun is already clear from context, own can stand alone after words like my or his, carrying the idea of possession without naming the object again.
senses.whyCN: 当名词已由上下文点明，own 可以跟在 my、his 这类物主词后单独使用，重复「属于」这层意思而不再说出物品的名字。

senses.title: To have something as property
senses.definition: to legally or actually have something as property
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上或事实上把某物作为财产持有
senses.example: Her family owns a small orchard outside the town.
senses.exampleCN: 她家在城外拥有一片小果园。
senses.why: The verb comes from the same Old English word for having and holding; possession is the plain centre that the adjective later uses to point at a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词来自同一个表示「持有、拥有」的古英语词；持有正是这个词最朴素的中心，形容词后来只是用它回指持有的人。

senses.title: To admit a fact or fault
senses.definition: to admit that something is true, especially something you would rather not say
senses.definitionCN: 承认某事为真，尤指本不愿说出口的事
senses.example: She owned that the plan had been too rushed.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认那个计划太仓促了。
senses.why: To own a fact is to accept it as part of what is yours, which is why British English uses own up for confessing a fault.
senses.whyCN: 承认一个事实，就是把它当成属于自己的东西接受下来；英式英语里 own up 表示坦白，正由此而来。

intro.en: Own has two faces: an Old English past participle meaning possessed, which became the adjective, and an Old English verb meaning to have, which became the modern verb.
intro.cn: own 有两副面孔：一个是表示「被拥有」的古英语过去分词，后来成了形容词；另一个是表示「持有」的古英语动词，后来成了今天的动词。

items.en: The adjective āgen was a past participle of the verb āgan and meant possessed or belonging to someone.
items.cn: 形容词 āgen 是动词 āgan 的过去分词，意为「被拥有的、属于某人的」。

items.en: The verb āgan meant to have, to hold and to own land or goods, and it is also the source of owe.
items.cn: 动词 āgan 意为持有、握着，拥有土地或财物，它同时也是 owe 的来源。

items.en: Middle English owen served as both adjective and verb, and the spelling with w replaced the old g sound in writing.
items.cn: 中古英语的 owen 同时作形容词和动词，书写上用 w 代替了旧的 g 音。

items.en: Own up appears in the sense of admitting a fault, extending possession to the idea of accepting a fact as one's own.
items.cn: own up 在十六世纪出现「承认过失」的意思，把「拥有」扩展到「把事实认作自己的」。

items.en: Modern English keeps own as adjective, pronoun and verb, while the related verb owe carries the debt side of the old word.
items.cn: 现代英语让 own 同时作形容词、代词和动词，而由同一旧词分出的 owe 承担了债务那一面。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the family built on this old verb of holding; the near-meaning group follows possession and, separately, the act of admitting.
note.cn: 形近组沿这个表示「持有」的旧动词所建的词族展开；近义组一面收「拥有」，一面收「承认」。

entries.definition: A person who owns something; own plus the person suffix -er.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物的人；own 加表示人的后缀 -er。

entries.definition: The state or legal right of owning something.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物的状态或法定权利。

entries.definition: To be in debt; it split from the same Old English verb as own.
entries.definitionCN: 欠债；与 own 由同一个古英语动词分出。

entries.definition: To have something, especially as property.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有某物，尤指作为财产。

entries.definition: To have something in your hands or under your control.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拿在手里，或置于自己控制之下。

entries.definition: To agree that something is true, often unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 承认某事为真，常带不情愿的意味。

normalIntro.en: The word carries both a pointing adjective and a holding verb, and the family around it keeps turning possession into people and rights.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词同时带着一个指认的形容词和一个持有的动词，它周围的词族不断把「拥有」变成人和权利。

normal.en: Āgan in Old English meant to have; both own and owe grew from it, one as possession, the other as debt.
normal.cn: 古英语 āgan 意为持有；own 与 owe 都由它长出，一个拿拥有，一个拿欠债。

normal.en: The -er on owner marks the person, while own itself marks the thing or the act.
normal.cn: owner 上的 -er 标出人，而 own 本身标出的是东西或动作。

normal.en: Own up is possession turned inward: you take a fault and call it yours.
normal.cn: own up 是拥有向内转：你把一个过失拿过来，说它是自己的。

normal.en: On your own means you are the only person in the picture, with nobody else to lean on.
normal.cn: on your own 意味着画面里只有你一个人，没有别人可以依靠。

normal.en: A room of your own is a place the possessive word cannot share with anyone else.
normal.cn: a room of your own 是一处物主词不肯与任何人分享的地方。

abstract.en: Owning is a social fact disguised as a grammar word: it always needs someone to point at.
abstract.cn: 拥有是一个装扮成语法词的社会事实：它总要指向某个人。

abstract.en: The same word for having and for confessing hints that admitting is a way of taking responsibility as yours.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既表示拥有又表示承认，暗示坦白就是把责任认领为自己的。

abstract.en: An owner is a name attached to a thing, and the thing may outlast the name.
abstract.cn: 所有者是附在物品上的一个名字，而物品往往比名字活得更久。

examples.en: She keeps her own keys in a small tin box.
examples.cn: 她把自己的钥匙放在一个小铁盒里。

examples.en: Her family owns a small orchard outside the town.
examples.cn: 她家在城外拥有一片小果园。

examples.en: She owned that the plan had been too rushed.
examples.cn: 她承认那个计划太仓促了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧恩」——钥匙上刻着自己的名字，一喊「欧恩」就知道是自己的门。

root: 古英语 āgan（持有）的过去分词 āgen 成为形容词「自己的」，同一动词又直接发展出动词「拥有」；「欠」义则由 owe 承担。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what belongs to a particular person; the adjective points at the owner, the pronoun leaves the noun unsaid, and the verb extends to holding property and to admitting a fault.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是属于某个特定之人的东西；形容词指向主人，代词省去名词，动词则扩展到持有财产与承认过失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key that fits one door and no other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把只配得上自家那扇门的钥匙。

branches.en: a name written inside a school coat
branches.cn: 校服内侧写着的名字

branches.en: a desk that nobody else may use
branches.cn: 不许别人用的那张书桌

branches.en: an orchard with a deed in a drawer
branches.cn: 抽屉里放着地契的果园

branches.en: a confession said out loud at last
branches.cn: 终于说出口的一句坦白

branches.en: a corner of a shared room marked by one chair
branches.cn: 公用房间里被一把椅子标出的角落

intro.en: Two Old English shapes meet in this word, a participle that became the adjective and a verb of holding; English suffixes then build the people and rights around it.
intro.cn: 这个词里汇合了两个古英语形态，一个成了形容词的分词，和一个表示持有的动词；英语后缀随后在它周围造出人与权利。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; its two grammatical lives both come from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的两种语法身份都来自古英语。

definition_zh: 实验；试验；尝试；做实验
definition_en: a test carried out under controlled conditions to discover or check something; also to carry out such a test, or to try something new
core_image: 两只同样的杯子并排放着，一只加了糖，一只没有，旁边一张纸上只写着一个待验证的问题
scene: 厨房桌上并排放着两只同样的杯子，一只加了糖，一只没加，旁边摊着一张写着待验证问题的纸。 The student ran the experiment twice to see whether the sugar changed the result.
sceneCN: 这里 experiment 指「在受控条件下检验某个设想的实验」（第 1 个义项：受控的科学检验）；句意为这名学生把实验做了两遍，看加糖是否改变了结果。图中可辨识物件：两只杯子、糖罐、记录纸、铅笔。

pos.zh: 实验；试验；（新事物的）尝试

derivatives.zh: 实验的；试验性的
实验；试验过程
实验者
以实验方式；在实验上
经过试验的

senses.title: A controlled scientific test
senses.definition: a procedure carried out under controlled conditions in order to test a hypothesis or discover a fact
senses.definitionCN: 为检验假设或发现事实而在受控条件下进行的操作
senses.example: The student ran the experiment twice to see whether the sugar changed the result.
senses.exampleCN: 这名学生把实验做了两遍，看加糖是否改变了结果。
senses.why: The core sense is a deliberate trial in which conditions are arranged so that one factor can be watched.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是有意的试验：把条件安排好，好让某一个因素被观察。

senses.title: A tentative attempt
senses.definition: an attempt made without assurance of success, in order to learn what happens
senses.definitionCN: 在并无成功把握的情况下做出尝试，只为看看会怎样
senses.example: Her first attempt at repairing the radio was an experiment rather than a repair.
senses.exampleCN: 她第一次修收音机，更像一次试验，而不是一次修理。
senses.why: Outside science the word keeps the same shape without the controls: you try something because you do not yet know the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 在科学之外，这个词保留了同样的形态，只是没有受控条件：你因为还不知道结果而去试一试。

senses.title: A set exercise in a teaching lab
senses.titleCN: 课堂上按规程做的实验
senses.definition: a prescribed practical exercise that students perform to see a known result for themselves
senses.definitionCN: 学生按既定规程操作、亲眼看到已知结果的一种练习
senses.example: The class does the same experiment with vinegar and baking soda every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 这个班每年秋天都做同一个醋与小苏打的实验。
senses.why: School labs repeat experiments whose answers are already known, so the word comes to mean the exercise rather than the inquiry.
senses.whyCN: 学校实验室重复的是答案已知的实验，于是这个词转而指那道练习，而非那次探究。

senses.title: A thought experiment
senses.definition: a scenario imagined in detail in order to test a principle that cannot be tried in reality
senses.definitionCN: 为检验无法在现实中操作的原理想象出来的详细情境
senses.example: Einstein's experiment with a falling elevator was carried out only in his head.
senses.exampleCN: 爱因斯坦那个关于下落电梯的实验只在头脑中进行。
senses.why: When the apparatus is imagination, the trial still keeps the name, because the point is still to test an idea.
senses.whyCN: 当器械换成想象时，这种试仍然沿用旧名，因为要点依旧是检验一个想法。

senses.title: An innovative departure
senses.titleCN: 在艺术或政策上的一次新尝试
senses.definition: a new way of doing something, tried in order to see whether it works better
senses.definitionCN: 为看清是否更好而尝试的一种新做法
senses.example: The theatre's experiment with a bare stage divided its critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这家剧院对空舞台的尝试使评论界分成两派。
senses.why: Any field that risks a new form borrows the word, since the new form is staked on an unknown outcome.
senses.whyCN: 任何冒险采用新形式的领域都会借用这个词，因为新形式押在一个未知的结果上。

senses.title: To carry out a scientific test
senses.definition: to perform a controlled test in order to gather evidence
senses.definitionCN: 为收集证据而进行受控检验
senses.example: They experimented on the alloy until they found its breaking point.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这种合金反复做实验，直到找出它的断裂点。
senses.why: The verb is simply the activity named by the noun, turned into something one does.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词所指的活动，转成一个人去做的事情。

senses.title: To try something out
senses.definition: to try a substance, method or style in order to learn its effects
senses.definitionCN: 为弄清效果而试用某种物质、方法或风格
senses.example: He experimented with colder water and the tea stopped tasting bitter.
senses.exampleCN: 他试着用更冷的水，茶就不再发苦了。
senses.why: The verb broadens from the laboratory to any deliberate trial of a variable.
senses.whyCN: 动词从实验室扩展开来，指对某一变量做的任何有意的试用。

senses.title: A venture in one's own life
senses.titleCN: 人生中的一次尝试（抽象义）
senses.definition: used of a period or venture in which someone tries a different way of living or working
senses.definitionCN: 指某人尝试另一种生活或工作方式的一段时期或一项事业
senses.example: Moving to the coast was an experiment in living more slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 搬到海边，是一次把日子过慢些的尝试。
senses.why: The abstract sense treats a life choice as a trial whose result cannot be known in advance.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把人生选择当作一场结果无法预知的试验。

intro.en: Experiment goes back to Latin experiri 'to try, test', whose noun experimentum meant 'a trial, a proof'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词可追溯到拉丁语 experiri「尝试、检验」，其名词 experimentum 意为「试、证明」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Periri meant 'to try, to attempt', and from the same stock came periculum 'trial, danger' and peritus 'experienced'. The link among them is generally accepted.
items.cn: periri 意为「尝试、试探」，同一词干还生出 periculum「试、危险」与 peritus「有经验的」。三者之间的关联一般认为是可靠的。

items.en: The prefix ex- 'out' added to periri gave experiri 'to try out, to test thoroughly', with the sense of carrying a trial through to its end.
items.cn: 前缀 ex-「向外」加 periri 构成 experiri「试出来、彻底检验」，带有把试验做到尽头的意思。

items.en: The noun experimentum named a trial, a proof or a piece of evidence, and also the experience gained from trying.
items.cn: 名词 experimentum 指一次试验、一项证明或一份证据，也指由尝试得来的经验。

items.en: English took the word in the fourteenth century through French, at first with the older sense of experience or observation rather than a staged procedure.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪经法语吸收这个词，最初取的是「经验、观察」的旧义，而非安排好的操作步骤。

items.en: From the seventeenth century, with the rise of organised investigation, the word settled into its present meaning of a controlled test of a hypothesis.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，随着有组织的探究兴起，这个词固定为今天「对假设作受控检验」的意思。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Latin form): the root behind periri is reconstructed, and though the family with peril and expert is widely accepted, no attested earlier form can be quoted.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拉丁语之前的形态）：periri 背后的词根属重构形式；尽管它与表示危险、有经验的同族关系被广泛接受，却没有可引用的更早实证形式。

note.en: Group one separates the near relatives built on the same Latin root; group two separates the ordinary words for a test.
note.cn: 第一组辨析同出拉丁词根的近亲；第二组辨析表示「检验」的常用词。

entries.definition: Built on the same verb for trying, but it means what one has lived through, not a staged test.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个表示尝试的动词，但指亲身经历过的事，而非安排好的检验。

entries.definition: From the adjective for 'experienced', so an expert is one who has tried things and learned; it names a person, not a procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示「有经验的」形容词，因此指试过并学到东西的人；它指人，不指程序。

entries.definition: From the noun for a trial that puts one at risk, so it survives only as the word for serious danger.
entries.definitionCN: 来自表示带风险的试的名词，因此只留下「严重危险」这一义。

entries.definition: The doer of an experiment; the difference from the noun is only the agent suffix, which is easy to miss in fast reading.
entries.definitionCN: 指做实验的人；与名词的差别只在表示施动者的后缀，快速阅读时容易看漏。

entries.definition: The general word for checking whether something works or is true; an experiment is its formal, scientific counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指检查某物是否有效或属实的词；experiment 是它正式、科学化的对应词。

entries.definition: A trial is a first use or run to see how something performs, often of a product or a method already made.
entries.definitionCN: 指为看某物表现如何而作的首次使用或试运行，多用于已经做成的产品或方法。

entries.definition: A study is a planned investigation, often longer and observational; not every study manipulates conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指有计划的调查，通常更长且偏观察；并非每项研究都操纵条件。

entries.definition: To probe is to investigate something hidden or unclear, often with repeated small inquiries rather than one designed trial.
entries.definitionCN: 指追查隐藏或不明之事，常用反复的小探询，而非一次设计好的试验。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is built from a Latin verb for trying plus a prefix meaning 'out', so it is a trying-out to the end.
normal.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「尝试」的动词加一个意为「向外」的前缀构成，因此是「试到底」。

normal.en: The same root gives peril and expert: a trial is risky, and one who has come through trials is experienced.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出「危险」与「有经验的」：试是有风险的，闯过许多试的人便有经验。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the method: carry out an experiment, a controlled experiment, experiment with a new method.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出方法：进行实验、对照实验、尝试新方法。

normal.en: The noun and the verb share one form, so the thing and the doing are the same word.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，因此这件事与做这件事是同一个词。

normal.en: A thought experiment keeps the name even when the apparatus is only imagination.
normal.cn: 思想实验即使器械只是想象，也仍沿用这个名字。

abstract.en: Picture two identical cups on a table, differing in exactly one spoonful.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两只一模一样的杯子，只差一勺东西。

abstract.en: Picture a lock with many keys, tried one at a time while someone writes down each result.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锁与许多钥匙，一把一把地试，旁边有人记下每次结果。

abstract.en: Picture a life lived for one year as a question rather than an answer.
abstract.cn: 想象把一年生活当作一个问题来过，而不是当作一个答案。

examples.en: The experiment showed that the plants grew faster in weak light.
examples.cn: 实验显示这些植物在弱光下长得更快。

examples.en: She experimented with three glazes before choosing one.
examples.cn: 她试了三种釉料才选定一种。

examples.en: No experiment on human subjects was allowed without consent.
examples.cn: 未经同意不得在人类受试者身上做实验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「试到底」：前缀表示向外，词根表示尝试，把一件事一直试到见结果 → 实验、尝试

root: 拉丁 experiri「尝试、检验」= ex-「向外」+ periri「试」；同族有 periculum「危险」与 peritus「有经验的」；experiri 的拉丁语之前形态属重构形式，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture, a deliberate trial: first the controlled test, then any tentative attempt, a classroom exercise, a trial run only in the mind, a new departure, the act of testing, trying a variable, and finally a life tried as an experiment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开，即有意的一次试：先是在受控条件下的检验，接着是任何试探性的尝试、课堂练习、只在头脑中进行的试、一种新做法、做实验这一行为、试用某个变量，最后把人生本身当作一次试验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two identical cups differing by one spoonful, and a written question waiting for an answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只只差一勺的相同杯子，以及一个等着答案的书面问题。

branches.en: The designed trial and the act of running it: the noun and the verb name one operation.
branches.cn: 设计好的试与执行这次试：名词与动词指同一操作。

branches.en: The loose attempt: trying something without guarantees, whether a repair or a colder cup of tea.
branches.cn: 宽松的试：在没有保证的情况下试，无论是修东西还是换冷水泡茶。

branches.en: The exercise and the imagined run: both repeat a known or imagined procedure for the sake of seeing.
branches.cn: 练习与想象中的试：两者都为「看见」而重演一个已知或设想的过程。

branches.en: The departure: a new form staked on an unknown outcome, in theatre or in policy.
branches.cn: 新做法：把新形式押在未知结果上，无论在剧场还是在政策上。

branches.en: The life trial: a year lived as a question rather than an answer.
branches.cn: 人生的试：把一年当作问题而非答案来过。

intro.en: Experiment is a Latin verb-noun pair in which a prefix, a root and a suffix each carry part of the meaning, and the same pieces build its English family.
intro.cn: 这个词是一组拉丁动词与名词，前缀、词根与后缀各担一部分意义，同样的部件也构成它的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin periri and its noun periculum supply the root; ex- adds the sense of carrying a trial through, and -mentum names the result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示「试」的动词与其名词提供词根；前缀增添「把试做到底」的意思，后缀则命名结果。

items.example: The prefix makes the trying exhaustive rather than casual.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使「试」成为彻底的，而非随意的。

items.example: The root carries the whole idea of a trial.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根承载「试」的全部意思。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into the record or result of a trial.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词转为一次试的记录或结果。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个合成动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The Latin noun already joins the act and its evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词已把行为与其证据合在一起。

items.example: English keeps one form for the thing and the doing.
items.exampleCN: 英语用同一个形式兼指这件事与做这件事。

items.example: The adjective marks whatever belongs to the testing stage.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记属于试验阶段的一切。

items.example: The noun names the practice rather than one trial.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指实践，而非某一次试。

items.example: The agent suffix names the person running the trial.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指执行这次试的人。

definition_zh: 国家；国土；乡村；郊区
definition_en: an area of land with its own government; land away from towns
core_image: 一片有自己的政府和边界的土地
scene: 升旗仪式上，我们大声唱着国歌，心里特别自豪。 Every student should love his or her country.
sceneCN: 这里 country 是「国家」（第 1 个义项：有政府、有边界的一片土地）；句意是每个学生都应热爱自己的国家。

derivatives.zh: 由 country 加 side 构成，义为「乡下；农村地区」
由 country 加 man 构成，义为「同胞；同乡」
拼写相近但来源不同，义为「郡；县」

senses.title: A nation with its own government
senses.definition: an area of land whose people have one government and usually share a language
senses.definitionCN: 一片土地，上面的人民由同一个政府管理，通常说同一种语言
senses.example: China is a large country with a long history.
senses.exampleCN: 中国是一个历史悠久的大国。
senses.why: The core image is a bordered land under one rule, so any such nation is a country.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一块有边界、由一个政权管理的土地，所以这样的国家都叫 country。

senses.title: Land away from towns
senses.definition: open land outside cities and towns, with fields and farms
senses.definitionCN: 城市之外有田野和农场的开阔地带
senses.example: We spent the weekend hiking in the country.
senses.exampleCN: 我们周末去乡下徒步了。
senses.why: From any big city, the whole land beyond the walls is the country, so the word also points to rural land.
senses.whyCN: 从任何大城市看，城墙之外的大地就是 the country，所以这个词也指乡村地区。

senses.title: The land or region itself
senses.definition: the land itself, especially when described by its features
senses.definitionCN: 土地本身，尤其用于描写地貌
senses.example: They drove through beautiful hilly country.
senses.exampleCN: 他们开车穿过美丽的丘陵地带。
senses.why: Because a country is first of all a piece of land, speakers also use it for land shaped by hills or rivers.
senses.whyCN: 因为 country 本义是土地，所以人们也用它指有山丘、河流特点的地带。

intro.en: Country comes from a Latin phrase about the land lying against something.
intro.cn: country 来自拉丁语短语，本义与「对着、位于对面的土地」有关。

items.en: The Latin phrase contra terram meant against the land, with contra meaning opposite.
items.cn: 拉丁语短语 contra terram 意为对着土地，contra 意为对面、相对。

items.en: Old French made cuntrée, meaning the region lying around, a district.
items.cn: 古法语造出 cuntrée，指周边的地区、地带。

items.en: English borrowed contree in the thirteenth century, meaning a district or area of land.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入 contree，指地区、土地。

items.en: Later it narrowed to mean the land of a nation with its own ruler.
items.cn: 后来词义收窄，指由自己君主统治的国家土地。

items.en: Today country means both a nation and, with the, rural land.
items.cn: 如今 country 既指国家，加定冠词时指乡村。

note.en: These words name lands and places, or sound close to country.
note.cn: 这些词都指土地与地方，或与 country 拼写读音相近。

entries.definition: rural land and scenery
entries.definitionCN: 乡下；农村风光

entries.definition: a district for local government; spelling differs, similar source
entries.definitionCN: 郡；县（拼写不同，来源相近）

entries.definition: someone from the same country or rural area
entries.definitionCN: 同胞；同乡

entries.definition: a table for service or to oppose; only sounds similar, different root
entries.definitionCN: 柜台；相反（读音相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a country and its people seen as a whole
entries.definitionCN: 国家；民族

entries.definition: a country or a political unit
entries.definitionCN: 国家；州

entries.definition: ground or a nation's territory
entries.definitionCN: 土地；国土

entries.definition: the countryside
entries.definitionCN: 农村地区

entries.definition: a small community in the country
entries.definitionCN: 村庄

normalIntro.en: Break the word into parts and connect each sense to a picture.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆开，给每个义项配一个画面。

normal.en: country = count + ry: count many nations, each is a country.
normal.cn: country 可联想 count（数）+ ry：数一数世界上有多少个国家。

normal.en: countryside keeps the whole word plus side: land at the side of towns.
normal.cn: countryside 就是整个词加 side：城市旁边的土地，即乡下。

normal.en: Plural rule: y changes to i, countries.
normal.cn: 复数规则：y 变 i 加 es，countries。

normal.en: In the country means in the countryside, not inside a nation.
normal.cn: in the country 指在乡下，不是在国家内部。

normal.en: Country music grew up among rural singers, hence the name.
normal.cn: 乡村音乐由乡村歌手唱红，所以得名 country music。

abstract.en: Picture a map with clear lines; every line holds one flag and one government.
abstract.cn: 想象画着清晰边界的地图，每条边界内有一面国旗、一个政府。

abstract.en: Outside the city wall, fields run to the horizon; that view is the country.
abstract.cn: 城墙外田野一直铺到天边，那片景色就是 the country。

abstract.en: Feel pride when the anthem plays; the feeling points at your country.
abstract.cn: 国歌响起时的自豪感，指向的就是你的国家。

examples.en: France is a European country famous for its food.
examples.cn: 法国是欧洲一个以美食闻名的国家。

examples.en: My grandparents live in the country, far from the noisy city.
examples.cn: 我祖父母住在乡下，离喧闹的城市很远。

examples.en: Athletes from every country joined the games.
examples.cn: 来自每个国家的运动员都参加了运动会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康川」——康庄大道通向一个个「国家」和乡川

root: 来自拉丁语 contra（对面）+ terra（土地），经古法语 cuntrée 进入英语，先指「周边地区」，后固定指「国家」；the country 特指乡村。

sensesIntro.en: From a bordered nation to open rural land, one word covers both.
sensesIntro.cn: 从有边界的国家到开阔的乡野，一个词覆盖两个意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a big piece of land with a border
core.cn: 核心意象：一块带边界的大土地

branches.en: A nation and its people
branches.cn: 国家及其人民

branches.en: Fields and farms outside towns
branches.cn: 城市外的田野与农场

branches.en: Land described by its scenery
branches.cn: 按地貌描写的地区

branches.en: Land first, nation second
branches.cn: 先是土地，后成国家

branches.en: Away-from-city views
branches.cn: 远离城市的景色

intro.en: Country hides an old Latin phrase inside its spelling.
intro.cn: country 的拼写里藏着一个古老的拉丁语短语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root terra means earth or land, as in territory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 terra 意为大地、土地，如 territory（领土）。

definition_zh: 豆；豆子；豆类植物；咖啡豆
definition_en: a seed of a climbing plant, used as food, or a seed that looks like it
core_image: 一把圆鼓鼓的豆子泡在清水里，慢慢涨大
scene: 做饭前，她把一杯干豆子倒进碗里，用水泡了一夜。 She soaked a cup of beans before making soup.
sceneCN: 这里 bean 是「豆子」（第 1 个义项：可食用的豆类种子）；句意为她做汤前泡了一杯豆子。

pos.zh: 名词：豆；豆子；豆类植物；咖啡豆

derivatives.zh: 由 bean 与 stalk 组合而成，义为「豆茎」
由 bean 与 bag 组合而成，义为「豆袋」
由 bean 与 pole 组合而成，义为「豆架」，口语中也指瘦高的人

senses.title: An edible seed
senses.definition: a seed from a climbing plant, cooked and eaten as food
senses.definitionCN: 藤本植物结出的种子，煮熟后作为食物
senses.example: She soaked a cup of beans before making soup.
senses.exampleCN: 她做汤前泡了一杯豆子。
senses.why: The word has named the edible seed since Old English, so the food itself is the centre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古英语起就指可食用的种子，所以食物本身是中心义。

senses.title: The plant that bears them
senses.definition: the plant that produces these seeds, often grown in fields
senses.definitionCN: 结出这种种子的植物，常在田里成片种植
senses.example: Farmers plant beans in spring and harvest them in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 农民春天种豆，夏天收获。
senses.why: As with many crops, the seed's name also names the plant that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 和许多作物一样，种子的名字也用来指结出它的植物。

senses.title: A seed of another plant
senses.definition: a seed of a different plant that looks like a bean, especially a coffee bean
senses.definitionCN: 外形像豆子的其他植物种子，尤指咖啡豆
senses.example: These coffee beans come from a small farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这些咖啡豆来自一个小农场。
senses.why: The shape is the link: any small oval seed can borrow the name of the familiar food.
senses.whyCN: 联系在形状：任何椭圆形的小种子都能借用这种熟悉食物的名字。

senses.title: A small amount, in negative phrases
senses.definition: a very small amount, used in phrases such as not know beans
senses.definitionCN: 极少的量，用于 not know beans 这类说法
senses.example: He does not know beans about fixing bikes.
senses.exampleCN: 他对修自行车一窍不通。
senses.why: A bean is small and cheap, so in negative phrases it stands for something almost worthless.
senses.whyCN: 豆子又小又便宜，所以在否定说法里它代表几乎不值一提的东西。

senses.title: Energy, in full of beans
senses.definition: in the phrase full of beans, full of energy and high spirits
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 full of beans，指精力旺盛、兴致很高
senses.example: The children were full of beans after the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行回来后孩子们精力充沛。
senses.why: Beans are solid, nourishing food, so a person full of them is pictured as full of energy.
senses.whyCN: 豆子是实在而有营养的食物，所以「装满豆子」的人就被想象成充满精力。

intro.en: Bean is an old Germanic word, and a related Latin word for the same plant survives as faba.
intro.cn: bean 是古老的日耳曼语词，拉丁语中表示同一种植物的相关词是 faba。

items.en: A reconstructed root for the bean plant lies behind both the Germanic and the Latin words.
items.cn: 一个可重构、指豆类植物的词根，是日耳曼语词与拉丁语词共同的远源。

items.en: Old English bean meant the edible seed, and the word kept that meaning without a break.
items.cn: 古英语 bean 指可食用的种子，这个词一直保留着这个意思。

items.en: Related forms in other Germanic languages confirm the shape of the old root.
items.cn: 其他日耳曼语中的相关形式印证了这一古老词根的形态。

items.en: English applied the word to coffee beans and other small oval seeds.
items.cn: 英语把这个词用到咖啡豆和其他椭圆形小种子上。

items.en: Informal phrases such as full of beans and not know beans add the later senses.
items.cn: full of beans 与 not know beans 这类口语说法带来了较晚的义项。

entries.definition: The plural of bean, used for many seeds or a dish of them.
entries.definitionCN: bean 的复数形式，指多颗豆子或一盘豆子。

entries.definition: The tall stem of a bean plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「豆茎」，由 bean 与 stalk 组合而成。

entries.definition: A soft bag filled with small beads, used as a seat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「豆袋坐垫」，由 bean 与 bag 组合而成。

entries.definition: A pole for beans to climb, or informally a very thin person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「豆架」，口语中也形容瘦高的人。

entries.definition: A small round green seed eaten as a vegetable; rounder than a bean.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「豌豆」，比豆子更圆，作蔬菜食用。

entries.definition: A small flat seed cooked in soups and stews.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小扁豆」，扁平小粒，常煮汤。

entries.definition: The general word for the part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「种子」，是这类可繁殖部分的总称。

entries.definition: The drink made from roasted beans; it names the product, not the seed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咖啡」，指烤过的豆子做成的饮品，而非种子本身。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root, the compounds, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语词根、复合词，以及这个词出现的短语。

normal.en: Bean has meant the edible seed since Old English, so the food sense is the oldest.
normal.cn: bean 从古英语起就指可食用的种子，所以食物义最古老。

normal.en: A beanstalk is what Jack climbed, and a beanpole is what the stalk grows on.
normal.cn: beanstalk 是杰克爬过的豆茎，beanpole 则是豆茎攀爬的支架。

normal.en: Coffee beans look like beans, which is why the shape gave them the name.
normal.cn: 咖啡豆外形像豆子，所以形状给了它们这个名字。

normal.en: Full of beans means full of energy, not full of food.
normal.cn: full of beans 意为精力充沛，而不是装满了豆子。

normal.en: Not know beans means to know nothing, because a bean is worth very little.
normal.cn: not know beans 意为一无所知，因为一颗豆子值不了什么。

abstract.en: Picture a dry bean in water: it swells quietly overnight, and that small change is the start of a meal.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗干豆泡在水里：一夜之间悄悄涨大，这点变化就是一顿饭的开始。

abstract.en: One seed holds a whole plant inside, which is why the same word names seed and plant.
abstract.cn: 一颗种子里面藏着一整株植物，所以同一个词既指种子也指植物。

abstract.en: Cheap, small, and nourishing, the bean becomes a picture of both energy and worthlessness in English phrases.
abstract.cn: 豆子便宜、小而有营养，在英语短语里既成了精力的象征，也成了「不值一提」的比喻。

examples.en: She soaked a cup of beans before making soup.
examples.cn: 她做汤前泡了一杯豆子。

examples.en: Farmers plant beans in spring and harvest them in summer.
examples.cn: 农民春天种豆，夏天收获。

examples.en: The children were full of beans after the trip.
examples.cn: 旅行回来后孩子们精力充沛。

root: bean 来自古英语 bean「可食用的豆」，源于日耳曼语 bauno，可上溯到原始印欧语中表示豆类植物的重构词根。拉丁语中同源的词是 faba「蚕豆」。词义由食用种子扩展到豆类植物，又用于咖啡豆等豆状种子。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of bean spread from one edible seed: the seed, the plant, other bean-shaped seeds, a tiny amount in negative phrases, and the energy that solid food suggests.
sensesIntro.cn: bean 的五个义项从一颗可食的种子扩展：种子、植物、其他豆状种子、否定说法里的「一点点」，以及实在食物所象征的精力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a handful of dry beans swells in a bowl of water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把干豆在清水碗里慢慢涨大。

branches.en: THE SEED: the word starts with the edible seed itself.
branches.cn: 种子线：这个词从可食用的种子本身开始。

branches.en: THE PLANT: the crop that carries the seed takes the same name.
branches.cn: 植物线：结出种子的作物用了同一个名字。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: any small oval seed can be called a bean.
branches.cn: 形状线：任何椭圆小种子都能叫 bean。

branches.en: THE SMALLNESS: a bean is cheap, so in negatives it means hardly anything.
branches.cn: 微小线：豆子便宜，所以在否定句里表示几乎不算什么。

branches.en: THE ENERGY: solid nourishing food becomes a picture of high spirits.
branches.cn: 精力线：实在而有营养的食物成了兴致高涨的比喻。

intro.en: Bean is an Old English root that forms compounds by placing the seed word first.
intro.cn: bean 是古英语词根，构词时把「豆」放在复合词前面。

latinIntro.en: Latin faba is a genuine cognate of bean, both going back to the same reconstructed root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 faba 是 bean 真正的同族词，两者都可上溯到同一个重构词根。

definition_zh: 顶部；顶端；盖子；首位；上衣；最上面的；顶部的；超过
definition_en: the highest part or point of something, or the best position, or the covering of a container
core_image: 一只手扶住梯子最上面那一级，脚下是整片屋顶
scene: 爬完最后一节梯子，屋顶就在眼前，风比街上大得多。 From the top of the hill you can see the whole harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 top 是「顶部、最高处」（第 1 个义项：物体的最高部分）；句意为从山顶上你能看到整个港湾。画面里有梯子顶端的横档、屋顶与远处的港湾。

pos.zh: 形容词：最上面的；最高的；顶尖的

derivatives.zh: 加复数词尾 -s，义为「顶部（复数）」，口语中也可作形容词「顶尖的」

加 -less 构成，义为「无顶的；无上装的」

senses.title: The highest part
senses.definition: the highest point or part of a thing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的最高处或最高部分
senses.example: A small flag was fixed to the top of the pole.
senses.exampleCN: 杆子的顶端系着一面小旗。
senses.why: The plain physical sense is the base from which lid, rank, and verb all later develop.
senses.whyCN: 这个最朴素的物理义项，是后来盖子、名次与动词各项含义所由发展的基础。

senses.title: A lid or cover
senses.definition: the cover of a container or bottle
senses.definitionCN: 容器或瓶子的封盖
senses.example: Screw the top back on before you shake it.
senses.exampleCN: 摇之前先把盖子拧回去。
senses.why: A lid closes a vessel at its top, so the word for the highest part names the cover too.
senses.whyCN: 盖子在容器顶端封口，于是表示最高部分的词也用来指盖子。

senses.title: The best or highest position
senses.definition: the leading place in a group, a list, or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 在群体、名单或行业中的领先位置
senses.example: She finished the season at the top of the rankings.
senses.exampleCN: 她在赛季结束时排名榜首。
senses.why: A ranking is a vertical list, so the person at the highest point of it is at the top.
senses.whyCN: 排名是一张竖着的名单，位于其最高点的人就在 top。

senses.title: A garment for the upper body
senses.definition: a piece of clothing worn on the upper body
senses.definitionCN: 穿在上身的衣物
senses.example: He put on a clean top and went down to dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他换上一件干净的上衣下楼吃饭。
senses.why: A top is the garment on the upper half of the body, and the word simply reuses the idea of the upper part.
senses.whyCN: top 指穿在上半身的衣物，这个词只是再次动用了「上部」这一概念。

senses.title: The highest in rank
senses.definition: as an adjective, highest in rank, quality, or position
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词时指等级、质量或位置最高的
senses.example: The matter is a top priority for the whole department.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事是整个部门的头等大事。
senses.why: The adjective is formed from the noun without any ending, which is common for short English words.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接由名词构成，不加任何词尾，这对英语短词很常见。

senses.title: To be higher than
senses.definition: to be greater in amount or degree than something else
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或程度上高出另者
senses.example: Sales topped two million copies in the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 首月销量超过了两百万册。
senses.why: A figure is like a mark on a pole, and to pass above it is to top it.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字像杆上的刻度，越过去就是 top it。

senses.title: To cover the surface of
senses.definition: to put something on the upper surface of food or of a structure
senses.definitionCN: 在食物或结构的上表面加上某物
senses.example: She topped the cake with thin slices of lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 她在蛋糕上铺了薄薄的柠檬片。
senses.why: Topping a dish is putting something on its upper surface, and the cooking verb keeps the meaning literal.
senses.whyCN: 给菜加浇头就是在它的上表面放东西，这个烹饪动词保留了字面意义。

senses.title: The head in informal speech
senses.definition: in informal speech, the head or hair on it
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指头顶或其上的头发
senses.example: He took his cap off and scratched the top of his head.
senses.exampleCN: 他摘下帽子挠了挠头顶。
senses.why: The informal head sense descends from the old word for a tuft of hair on the crown.
senses.whyCN: 口语中的「头顶」义来自那个表示头顶发簇的古词。

senses.title: A spinning toy
senses.definition: a toy that spins on a point, an older sense kept in the word's history
senses.definitionCN: 一种以尖端着地旋转的玩具，是这个词较早的义项
senses.example: The spinning toy is a separate word that happens to share the spelling, and it survives in the modern language only in this narrow use.
senses.exampleCN: 这种旋转玩具有自己的词源，只是恰好同形，今天只在极窄的用法里留存。
senses.why: The toy turns on a single point at its bottom, so the shape of a top on a point links the two words by accident of form.
senses.whyCN: 陀螺以底部的一个尖点旋转，于是「尖顶」之形与它偶然相连，成了同形的两个词。

intro.en: Top is an Old English word for the highest part, and an older separate sense names a spinning top; the two senses were probably never the same word.
intro.cn: top 在古英语中表示最高部分；另一个更早的义项指陀螺，两者很可能从来不是同一个词。

items.en: Top names the summit or the highest point, and is used of hills, trees, and buildings.
items.cn: 古英语 top 指顶巅或最高点，用于山、树与建筑。

items.en: A separate word topp names a tuft of hair on the head, which explains the informal sense of the head.
items.cn: 另有一个词 topp 指头上一簇头发，这解释了口语中「头顶」的义项。

items.en: Old Norse toppr and Old High German zopf all mean a summit or a tuft.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 toppr 与古高地德语 zopf 都表示顶或发簇。

items.en: Middle English applies top to lids and covers, since a lid sits at the top of a vessel.
items.cn: 中古英语把 top 用于盖子，因为盖正位于容器的顶上。

items.en: The verb to top appears in the sixteenth century with the sense of putting something on the upper surface.
items.cn: 动词 top 于十六世纪出现，义为在表面之上放东西。

items.en: The sense of surpassing comes in the seventeenth century, from the idea of going above a mark.
items.cn: 「超过」之义于十七世纪出现，源自越过某个标记的想法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short forms built on the same stem, while the near-meaning group gathers words for summit, cover, and ranking.
note.cn: 形近组收集同一词干构成的短形式，近义组则汇集表示顶部、盖子与名次的词。

normal.en: Top of is a position, on top of is contact, and the particle changes the picture.
normal.cn: top of 是位置，on top of 是接触，介词改变了画面。

normal.en: Top priority puts the adjective before the noun and means first in importance.
normal.cn: top priority 把形容词放在名词前，意为最重要。

normal.en: From top to bottom goes through a thing completely, from the first layer to the last.
normal.cn: from top to bottom 从第一层到最后一层，指彻底贯穿。

normal.en: Bottle top and pen top both mean the cover, because a cover sits where the top is.
normal.cn: bottle top 与 pen top 都指盖子，因为盖就在顶处。

normal.en: The verb to top means to rise above a figure, as in sales topped a million.
normal.cn: 动词 top 意为高于某个数字，如销量过百万。

abstract.en: Picture a hand flat on the very last rung, with nothing above it but sky.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在最后一级横档上，上面只剩天空。

abstract.en: Think of a list where one name sits alone above all the others.
abstract.cn: 想一张名单，有一个名字单独居于所有名字之上。

abstract.en: A top closes a thing, ranks a thing, and beats a thing, and all three come from being highest.
abstract.cn: 顶能封住一物、排出一物、也高过一物，三者都源自「在最上」。

examples.en: There is a bird's nest at the top of the tree.
examples.cn: 树顶有一个鸟巢。

examples.en: The film topped the box office for three weeks.
examples.cn: 这部电影连续三周位居票房榜首。

definition_en: relating to a paid occupation, or showing the skill and standards expected in one
core_image: 一件熨得笔挺的白大褂，胸口别着写有姓名的工牌
scene: 手术室里，主刀医生动作稳而快。 Every step was measured and every cut was clean, and the assistant called that level of care professional.
sceneCN: 这里 professional 是「专业的、达到职业水准的」（第 3 个义项：具备职业所需的技能与规范）；句意：每一步都经过斟酌，每一刀都干净利落，助手把这种水准称为专业。图中可辨识物件：手术台、无影灯、器械盘、白大褂、工牌；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Relating to a profession
senses.definition: connected with a profession or its members
senses.definitionCN: 与某个职业或其成员相关
senses.example: professional bodies set entry exams.
senses.exampleCN: 行业机构设置入行考试。
senses.why: Profession comes from Latin professio, 'a public declaration'. A professional was first someone who had publicly declared a calling, which is why the word implies a recognized field.
senses.whyCN: profession 来自拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”。professional 最初指公开宣告某种志业的人，所以这个词隐含一个被承认的领域。

senses.title: Done as a paid occupation
senses.definition: engaged in for payment rather than as a hobby
senses.definitionCN: 为报酬而从事，而非作为爱好
senses.example: She is a professional musician.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一名职业音乐家。
senses.why: The 18c. sharpened the contrast with amateur: a professional is paid, an amateur is not. Money becomes the marker that separates the two.
senses.whyCN: 18 世纪强化了与 amateur 的对比：professional 拿钱，业余者不拿。金钱成了区分两者的标记。

senses.title: Competent and skillful
senses.definition: showing the skill and care expected of a trained person
senses.definitionCN: 表现出受训者应有的技能与用心
senses.example: That was a very professional repair job.
senses.exampleCN: 那次维修做得非常专业。
senses.why: Skill turns the label into a compliment: work is professional when it meets the standard a paying client would expect. The word moves from status to quality.
senses.whyCN: 技能把这个标签变成赞美：当工作达到付费客户期待的标准，它就是专业的。这个词从身份转向品质。

senses.title: A member of a profession
senses.definition: a person who works in a profession, especially a learned one
senses.definitionCN: 从事某一职业的人，尤指需要专门学识者
senses.example: The panel included doctors and other professionals.
senses.exampleCN: 专家组包括医生及其他专业人员。
senses.why: The noun names the person behind the adjective. In modern English it often covers lawyers, doctors, engineers, and accountants — fields with entry rules and codes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名形容词背后的人。现代英语中它常涵盖律师、医生、工程师、会计师——有准入规则与职业准则的领域。

senses.title: An expert in a field
senses.definition: a person with high skill in some activity
senses.definitionCN: 在某项活动中技能很高的人
senses.example: He is a professional when it comes to chess.
senses.exampleCN: 在国际象棋上他是个行家。
senses.why: The word can leave the salaried professions behind and simply mean 'someone who really knows'. This looser use turns expertise itself into the qualification.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以离开领薪的职业，只表示“真正懂行的人”。这种宽松用法把专长本身当成资格。

senses.title: A paid sports player
senses.definition: in sport, a player who is paid to compete
senses.definitionCN: 体育中受薪参赛的选手
senses.example: He turned professional at nineteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十九岁转为职业选手。
senses.why: Sport copied the paid/amateur divide. Turning professional means crossing a line: from playing for love to playing for a living, with different rules and stakes.
senses.whyCN: 体育复制了“受薪／业余”的分界。转为职业，意味着跨过一条线：从为热爱而赛，到为生计而赛，规则与利害都不同。

senses.title: Conforming to professional standards
senses.definition: behaving with the ethics and manners of a profession
senses.definitionCN: 以某职业的伦理与礼节行事
senses.example: Her response was calm and professional.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回应冷静而专业。
senses.why: Conduct is judged, not skill. The word can praise someone who keeps confidences and meets deadlines, even when the task is routine.
senses.whyCN: 这里被评判的是行为，不是技能。即使任务平常，这个词也能赞美守密、守时的人。

senses.title: Of high quality, informally
senses.definition: in informal use, well-made or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法：做得好的、像样的
senses.example: They did a professional job on the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把花园弄得相当像样。
senses.why: The compliment has spread beyond occupations: anything done with care can look professional. The word now sells quality as much as status.
senses.whyCN: 这种赞美已超出职业范围：任何用心做成的事都可能显得 professional。这个词现在既卖身份，也卖品质。

senses.title: A euphemism for a sex worker (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, a euphemism for a prostitute
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：对妓女的委婉说法
senses.example: The old novel refers to her as a professional.
senses.exampleCN: 那部旧小说用 professional 指称她。
senses.why: The 'paid occupation' sense sits close to a taboo, so the euphemism was available. Modern usage avoids it because the main sense has become too respectable to carry the hint.
senses.whyCN: “受薪职业”义接近禁忌，因此这个委婉说法曾可用。现代用法避开它，因为主要义已太体面，承载不了这层暗示。

intro.en: Professional is built on profession, and profession began as a public declaration. Latin profiteri means 'declare openly', from pro- 'forth' plus fateri 'to confess'. A professional is, etymologically, someone who has declared what they do.
intro.cn: professional 建立在 profession 上，而 profession 始于“公开宣告”。拉丁语 profiteri 意为“公开宣称”，由 pro-“向前、出来”加 fateri“承认”构成。从词源看，professional 就是公开宣告自己以何为业的人。

items.en: First recorded as an adjective meaning 'of or belonging to a profession'.
items.cn: 最早记录为形容词，义为“属于某一职业的”。

items.en: profession (late 14c.) comes from Latin professionem, 'a public declaration', from profiteri 'declare openly'.
items.cn: profession（14 世纪末）来自拉丁语 professionem“公开宣告”，源出 profiteri“公开宣称”。

items.en: profiteri = pro- 'forth, publicly' + fateri 'to confess, admit'. The root fateri also gives confession and fate in related senses.
items.cn: profiteri = pro-“向外、公开”+ fateri“承认、告白”。词根 fateri 还生成 confession 等相关词。

items.en: The sense 'engaged in a profession as a paid calling' is recorded.
items.cn: “以某职业为受薪志业”的义项被记录。

items.en: The noun professional appears for a person who makes a living by a profession.
items.cn: 名词 professional 出现，指以某职业谋生的人。

items.en: Modern English extends the adjective from occupations to quality and conduct: professional advice, professional standards, a professional job.
items.cn: 现代英语把形容词从职业扩展到品质与行为：professional advice、professional standards、a professional job。

note.en: The first group shares the profession/profiteri stem; the second is about words that also mean skilled or paid.
note.cn: 第一组共享 profession/profiteri 词干，第二组看同样表示“有技能”或“受薪”的词。

entries.definition: a paid occupation requiring training. It is the noun behind professional.
entries.definitionCN: 需要训练的受薪职业。它是 professional 背后的名词。

entries.definition: the standards and conduct of a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 职业标准与职业精神。

entries.definition: a university teacher, literally one who professes a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 大学教授，字面“宣称某学科者”。

entries.definition: a person with special knowledge. It stresses knowledge, not pay or code.
entries.definitionCN: 有专门知识的人。它强调知识，而非报酬或准则。

entries.definition: having trained ability. It says nothing about a profession or payment.
entries.definitionCN: 受过训练、有能力。它不涉及职业或报酬。

entries.definition: relating to a job. It is neutral and technical, unlike the status-laden professional.
entries.definitionCN: 与工作相关的。它中性、技术性，不像 professional 带身份色彩。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin profiteri 'declare openly', the paid/amateur divide, the professional/professor family, and the modern quality sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 profiteri“公开宣称”、受薪／业余之分、professional/professor 词族，以及现代品质义。

normal.en: Latin profiteri means 'declare openly': a professional has publicly declared what they do.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 profiteri 意为“公开宣称”：professional 已公开宣告自己以何为业。

normal.en: The 18c. made money the test: professionals are paid, amateurs are not.
normal.cn: 18 世纪以金钱为标准：professional 受薪，业余者不受薪。

normal.en: Professor and professional share the root: both publicly profess a field.
normal.cn: professor 与 professional 共享词根：两者都公开宣称某个领域。

normal.en: The word has moved from status to quality: a professional job is simply a job done to a high standard.
normal.cn: 这个词从身份滑向品质：a professional job 就是做得高标准的工作。

normal.en: In sport, turning professional means crossing from playing for love to playing for a living.
normal.cn: 体育中，转为职业意味着从为热爱而赛，跨到为生计而赛。

abstract.en: A profession is a public promise: the declaration is what binds the practitioner to a code.
abstract.cn: 职业是一份公开承诺：宣告把从业者绑定到一套准则上。

abstract.en: Professionalism is a form of trust infrastructure: strangers can rely on you because a field vouches for you.
abstract.cn: 专业精神是一种信任基础设施：陌生人能依赖你，因为一个领域为你背书。

abstract.en: When the word praises quality rather than occupation, it shows how deeply work and identity are fused in modern life.
abstract.cn: 当这个词赞美品质而非职业时，它显示出工作与身份在现代生活中融合得有多深。

examples.en: You should seek professional advice before investing.
examples.cn: 投资前你应当寻求专业建议。

examples.en: She handled the complaint in a professional manner.
examples.cn: 她以专业的方式处理了这起投诉。

examples.en: He became a professional football player at twenty.
examples.cn: 他二十岁时成为职业足球运动员。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑若费神”——为了职业扑上去费神打磨 → professional 职业的、专业的

root: 由 profession + -al 构成；profession 来自拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”，源出 profiteri“公开宣称”= pro-“向外”+ fateri“承认”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of professional, all built on a public declaration. The declaration can name an occupation, mark payment, certify skill, impose conduct, or simply advertise quality.
sensesIntro.cn: professional 的九个义项都建立在一次公开宣告上。这次宣告可以命名职业、标记受薪、证明技能、施加行为准则，或仅仅为品质作广告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a public declaration that binds a person to a standard.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次公开宣告，把人绑定到某个标准上。

branches.en: FIELD: a recognized occupation and the people who belong to it.
branches.cn: 领域：被承认的职业及其成员。

branches.en: PAY: the paid/amateur line, in work and in sport.
branches.cn: 报酬：工作与体育中的受薪／业余分界。

branches.en: SKILL: training shows as competence, and competence can stand alone as expertise.
branches.cn: 技能：训练表现为胜任，胜任又可单独成为专长。

branches.en: ETHICS: conduct is judged by the standards of the field.
branches.cn: 伦理：行为按该领域的标准被评判。

branches.en: EXTENSIONS: informal praise of quality, and an archaic euphemism that the main sense has outgrown.
branches.cn: 延伸：对品质的非正式赞美，以及主要义已使其不再适用的旧委婉语。

intro.en: Professional is profession plus -al. English adds -ly, -ism, -ize, and the negative un-, while the Latin fateri also gives confess and confession.
intro.cn: professional 是 profession 加 -al。英语加 -ly、-ism、-ize 与否定 un-，拉丁语 fateri 还生成 confess 与 confession。

latinIntro.en: Latin professio 'public declaration' and profiteri 'declare openly' combine pro- 'forth' with fateri 'admit'. The family is about public avowal, not merely employment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 professio“公开宣告”与 profiteri“公开宣称”把 pro-“向外”与 fateri“承认”结合。这个词族关乎公开表态，而不只是就业。

items.meaning: the standards and spirit of a profession
to make an activity a recognized profession
the process of becoming a profession
a paid occupation; a public declaration
items.meaningCN: 职业；公开宣告（同族名词）

items.meaning: to declare openly; to claim a belief
items.meaningCN: 公开宣称；信奉（同族动词）

items.meaning: to admit a fault or truth

definition_en: to close something, to stop operating, to block, or to keep someone or something inside

scene: 请把门关上。 Please shut the door.
sceneCN: 这里 shut 是「关上」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把门关上。

derivatives.zh: 停业；关机
百叶窗；快门
闭门不出的人
零封

senses.title: To close
senses.definition: to close a door, window, or container
senses.definitionCN: 关上门、窗或容器
senses.example: Please shut the door.
senses.exampleCN: 请把门关上。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To stop operating
senses.definition: to close a business or machine
senses.definitionCN: 关闭企业或机器
senses.example: The factory shut last month.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂上个月停业了。
senses.why: A closed place stops working like a closed door.
senses.whyCN: 关闭的场所像关上的门一样停止运作。

senses.title: To block
senses.definition: to block an opening or a view
senses.definitionCN: 挡住开口或视线
senses.example: The curtain shuts out the light.
senses.exampleCN: 窗帘把光挡住了。
senses.why: Closing can mean keeping something out.
senses.whyCN: 关闭也可以表示把某物挡在外面。

senses.title: To confine
senses.definition: to keep someone or something inside
senses.definitionCN: 把某人或某物关在里面
senses.example: They shut the dog in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把狗关在院子里。
senses.why: Closing can also keep something in.
senses.whyCN: 关闭也可以表示把某物关在里面。

intro.en: Shut comes from an Old English verb for bolting a door.
intro.cn: shut 来自古英语中表示给门上门闩的动词。

items.en: Scyttan meant to bolt or bar a door.
items.cn: scyttan 意为给门上门闩或横闩。

items.en: Shutten widened to mean to close.
items.cn: shutten 扩大为表示关闭。

items.en: The word covered windows and containers.
items.cn: 这个词覆盖了窗户和容器。

items.en: Businesses could shut for the day.
items.cn: 企业可以当天停业。

items.en: Shut in and shut out split the idea of closure.
items.cn: shut in 与 shut out 分化了关闭的方向。

note.en: Shut is compared with similar-looking words and with words for closing.
note.cn: 把 shut 与形近词以及表示关闭的词作比较。

entries.definition: to call loudly
entries.definitionCN: 喊叫

entries.definition: a firing or photograph
entries.definitionCN: 射击；照片

entries.definition: to raise the shoulders

entries.definition: to shut something
entries.definitionCN: 关闭

entries.definition: to close tightly
entries.definitionCN: 密封

entries.definition: to fasten with a key
entries.definitionCN: 锁上

normalIntro.en: To shut is to make an opening stop being open.
normalIntro.cn: shut 就是让一个开口不再敞开。

normal.en: Please shut the door.
normal.cn: 请把门关上。

normal.en: The factory shut last month.

normal.en: The curtain shuts out the light.

normal.en: They shut the dog in the yard.

normal.en: Shut the window before you leave.

abstract.en: A shut door is a promise of privacy.
abstract.cn: 关上的门是隐私的承诺。

abstract.en: Shutting out noise can be a kindness.
abstract.cn: 把噪声挡在外面也可以是一种善意。

abstract.en: Some doors must shut before others open.
abstract.cn: 有些门必须先关上，别的门才会打开。

examples.en: Please shut the door.

dict_mnemonic.text: shut 的核心是「合上」：门合上是关门，厂子合上是停业，帘子合上就把光挡在外面。

root: 源自古英语 scyttan（上门闩），核心义「合拢、封闭开口」。

sensesIntro.en: Shut means to close, to stop operating, to block, or to confine.
sensesIntro.cn: shut 意为关上、停业、挡住或关住。

core.en: Closing an opening so that passage stops.
core.cn: 合上开口，使通行停止。

branches.en: The door meets its frame.
branches.cn: 门与门框合上。

branches.en: The business stops its work.
branches.cn: 企业停止运作。

branches.en: Light and sound stay outside.
branches.cn: 光和声音被留在外面。

branches.en: What is inside stays inside.
branches.cn: 里面的东西留在里面。

branches.en: Closing works in both directions.
branches.cn: 关闭在两个方向上都起作用。

intro.en: Shut builds a family of closure words.
intro.cn: shut 构成表示封闭的词族。

latinIntro.en: Shut is Germanic; Latin claudere, to close, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shut 属日耳曼语；拉丁语 claudere（关闭）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: a closing of a business or machine
a person who rarely goes out

items.meaning: a game where one side scores nothing
