definition_zh: 饼干；小点心；浅褐色
definition_en: a small flat baked cake, crisp in British use and soft in American use
core_image: 一盘刚出炉的脆饼，边缘微微焦黄
scene: 下午茶时间，奶奶把一块脆饼掰成两半，放进茶杯里蘸了蘸。 She dunked a biscuit in her tea.
sceneCN: 这里 biscuit 是「饼干」（第 1 个义项：英式脆饼）；句意为她把一块饼干蘸进茶里。

pos.zh: 名词：饼干；小点心；浅褐色

derivatives.zh: 由 biscuit 加 -y 构成，义为「饼干般的；饼干味的」
同源借词，来自意大利语，义为「意大利脆饼」

senses.title: The crisp baked cake
senses.definition: a small flat cake baked until crisp, eaten with tea or as a snack
senses.definitionCN: 一种小而扁的糕点，烤至酥脆，配茶或作零食食用
senses.example: She dunked a biscuit in her tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一块饼干蘸进茶里。
senses.why: Latin bis coctus means twice cooked, and the crisp British biscuit is exactly bread baked twice to drive the moisture out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 bis coctus 意为「烤两次」，而英式脆饼正是经过两次烘烤、把水分逼干的饼。

senses.title: A soft quick bread
senses.definition: in American English, a small soft bread similar to a scone, often eaten with gravy
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语中指类似司康的小型软面包，常配肉汁吃
senses.example: She baked biscuits for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她烤了小软饼当早饭。
senses.why: American cooks used the borrowed word for a soft quick bread, so the same spelling names two quite different baked goods.
senses.whyCN: 美国厨师用这个借来的词来指一种软质的快手面包，于是同一个拼写指两种颇为不同的烘焙食品。

senses.title: A pale brown colour
senses.definition: a pale warm brown colour like a baked biscuit
senses.definitionCN: 像烤好的饼干那样浅而暖的褐色
senses.example: The walls were painted biscuit.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成了浅褐色。
senses.why: Food words often become colour words, and the warm baked tone of a biscuit gave this paint and fabric shade its name.
senses.whyCN: 食物名称常常变成颜色名称，饼干那种温暖的烘焙色就给了这种涂料与布料色调一个名字。

intro.en: Biscuit is a Latin phrase that travelled through French and split into two national meanings in English.
intro.cn: biscuit 是一个经法语传入英语的拉丁语短语，在英语里分成了两种国别用法。

items.en: Latin bis coctus meant twice cooked, describing bread baked twice so that it would keep.
items.cn: 拉丁语 bis coctus 意为「烤两次」，描述为便于保存而烘烤两遍的面包。

items.en: Old French bescuit carried the same twice-baked idea across the Channel.
items.cn: 古法语 bescuit 把同一个「烤两次」的意思带过了海峡。

items.en: Early English spellings varied, and the form biscuit eventually settled.
items.cn: 早期英语拼写有多种，最终固定为 biscuit。

items.en: British English kept the crisp meaning, while American English applied the word to a soft quick bread.
items.cn: 英式英语保留「脆」的意思，美式英语则把这个词用于一种软质的快手面包。

items.en: The pale baked colour of a biscuit gave the word a third sense for paint and cloth.
items.cn: 饼干那种浅淡的烘焙色，给这个词添了第三个义项，用于涂料与布料。

items.en: Today biscuit is a snack word in Britain and a breakfast bread word in America.
items.cn: 今天 biscuit 在英国是零食词，在美国则是早餐面食词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the same-origin Italian word and similar sounds; the near-meaning group collects other baked snacks.
note.cn: 形近组收同源的意大利语词与读音相近的词；近义组收其他烘焙点心。

entries.definition: Italian crisp biscuits, baked twice like the original Latin name says.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「意大利脆饼」，与拉丁语原名一样经过两次烘烤。

entries.definition: To cut something into two equal parts.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「平分、对切」，与 biscuit 共享表示「二」的前缀。

entries.definition: A container made of woven material.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「篮子」，读音与 biscuit 相近。

entries.definition: A small sweet cake, the usual American word for a biscuit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「曲奇饼干」，是美式英语里对饼干的常用说法。

entries.definition: A thin dry biscuit that snaps when broken.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薄脆饼」，掰开时会发出脆响。

entries.definition: A small round cake of flour and fat, often eaten with tea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「司康饼」，一种面粉与油脂做的小圆饼，常配茶。

entries.definition: A very thin crisp biscuit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「威化薄饼」，一种极薄的脆饼。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Latin phrase, the real relatives, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的拉丁短语、真实同源词和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Bis means twice and coctus means cooked, so a biscuit is bread cooked twice.
normal.cn: bis 表示「两次」，coctus 表示「煮熟的」，所以 biscuit 就是「烤两遍的饼」。

normal.en: Italian biscotti keeps the same Latin idea and the same crisp texture.
normal.cn: 意大利语 biscotti 保留了同样的拉丁观念和同样的脆质地。

normal.en: Britain eats crisp biscuits with tea, while America bakes soft biscuits for breakfast.
normal.cn: 英国人配茶吃脆饼干，美国人则把软饼当早餐。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with tin, crumbs, chocolate and tea.
normal.cn: 它常与 tin、crumbs、chocolate、tea 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-i-s-c-u-i-t: the ui pair sits in the middle and is easy to drop.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-i-s-c-u-i-t，中间的 ui 组合很容易漏写。

abstract.en: See a tray of pale golden rounds just out of the oven: that is biscuit.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘刚出炉的浅金色圆饼，那就是 biscuit。

abstract.en: Soften the same round into a breakfast bread and the word changes nationality.
abstract.cn: 把同一个圆饼变软成早餐面包，这个词就换了国别用法。

abstract.en: Say the word, then let the warm tray bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那盘温热的饼把意思带回来。

examples.en: She dunked a biscuit in her tea.
examples.cn: 她把一块饼干蘸进茶里。

examples.en: She baked biscuits for breakfast.
examples.cn: 她烤了小软饼当早饭。

examples.en: The walls were painted biscuit.
examples.cn: 墙壁被刷成了浅褐色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「必是吃的」——下午茶必备，必是吃的：饼干

root: biscuit 来自拉丁语 bis coctus「烤两次」，经古法语 bescuit 进入英语，指为便于保存而烘烤两遍的面包。英式英语保留了「脆」的意思，美式英语则用它指一种软质快手面包；饼干那种浅淡的烘焙色又给这个词添了「浅褐色」义。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses of biscuit all start at the same oven: a twice-baked cake, the soft American version, and the warm colour it takes on.
sensesIntro.cn: biscuit 的三个义项都从同一个烤炉出发：烤两次的饼、美式软饼，以及它烤出来的暖色调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tray of pale golden rounds fresh from the oven
core.cn: 核心意象：一盘刚出炉的浅金色圆饼

branches.en: THE CRISP ONE: twice-baked bread is the British biscuit dipped in tea.
branches.cn: 脆饼线：烤两次的面包就是配茶吃的英式饼干。

branches.en: THE SOFT ONE: American cooks applied the same word to a quick soft bread.
branches.cn: 软饼线：美国厨师把同一个词用在了软质快手面包上。

branches.en: THE COLOUR: the baked tone of the crust became a paint and cloth shade.
branches.cn: 颜色线：饼皮的烘焙色成了涂料与布料的色调。

branches.en: THE SAME CRUST: what you eat and what you see share one warm surface.
branches.cn: 同一层皮：你吃的东西与你看到的颜色共用一层暖色表面。

branches.en: THE TWO TONGUES: one borrowed word grew two different foods in two countries.
branches.cn: 两种语言线：一个借词在两个国家长成两种不同的食品。

intro.en: Biscuit is a borrowed compound of two Latin parts; the items below show those parts and the family around it.
intro.cn: biscuit 是由两个拉丁成分构成的借词，下面列出的是这些成分以及它周围的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin bis and coctus are the two recorded elements behind this word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 bis 与 coctus 是这个词背后两个有记录的成分。

items.example: It is the first element of the Latin phrase behind biscuit.
items.exampleCN: 它是 biscuit 背后那个拉丁短语的第一个成分。

items.example: It is the second element of that Latin phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它是那个拉丁短语的第二个成分。

items.example: He took a biscuit from the tin.
items.exampleCN: 他从罐子里拿了一块饼干。
它把 biscotto 变成 biscotti。

definition_zh: 除非；如果不；除非在……情况下
definition_en: except if; used to say that something will happen only if another thing does not happen
core_image: 一个岔路口立着一块牌子：除非走左边，否则到不了目的地；右边是一条被挡住的路
scene: 教练在雨天早晨对队员说，只有雨停才训练，否则全体在馆里看录像。 We will not play outside unless the rain stops by noon.
sceneCN: 这里 unless 是「除非」（第 1 个义项：表示只有在某条件不成立时才发生）；句意为除非中午前雨停，否则我们不在外面踢球。路口那块牌子划出的唯一通路，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 除非；如果不（引导条件从句）
除……之外（少见，多见于书面）
除非在……的情况下（与 not 连用表双重否定）

collocations.zh: 除非……否则什么也不会发生

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「带 unless 从句的」
由古英语 þy læs þe 缩合而成，义为「以免」，是 unless 的老近亲
与本词同源，义为「较少的」，构成 unless 的后半

senses.title: Except if
senses.definition: except if; a condition that alone can change the result
senses.definitionCN: 「除非」；唯一能够改变结果的那个条件
senses.example: You cannot enter unless you show your ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 除非出示门票，否则你不能进场。
senses.why: Unless is a compressed on less: the case you name is the single exception to the statement.
senses.whyCN: unless 是 on less 的压缩：你提出的那种情形是对这句话的唯一例外。

senses.title: Only in that case
senses.definition: used after a negative or in a question to mean only if
senses.definitionCN: 用于否定句或疑问句之后，意为「只有在……才」
senses.example: I will not agree unless the whole plan is explained first.
senses.exampleCN: 除非先把整个计划解释清楚，否则我不会同意。
senses.why: With not in front, the exception becomes the one door left open.
senses.whyCN: 前面加了 not，这个例外就成了唯一还开着的门。

senses.title: Except for
senses.definition: in older or formal prose, except for a thing just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在较早或正式的书面语中，指「除了刚提到的某物」
senses.example: Nothing was left of the house unless the stone steps.
senses.exampleCN: 除了那几级石阶，这座房子什么也没有剩下。
senses.why: The very old prepositional use keeps the plain sense of less as leaving something out.
senses.whyCN: 很古老的介词用法保留着 less「除去」的朴素含义。

senses.title: In fixed legal phrases
senses.definition: in clauses such as unless otherwise stated, the rule applies except where noted
senses.definitionCN: 在 unless otherwise stated 一类条款中，表示除注明处之外规则一律适用
senses.example: The fee is paid yearly unless otherwise agreed in writing.
senses.exampleCN: 除非另有书面约定，费用按年支付。
senses.why: Contracts need a single word for the written exception, and this is that word.
senses.whyCN: 合同需要一个词专门表示书面的例外，用的就是这个词。

senses.title: Doubled for emphasis
senses.definition: in the phrase unless and until, meaning not before at the earliest
senses.definitionCN: 在 unless and until 这一说法中，意为「最早也要到……才行」
senses.example: The office stays closed unless and until the roof is repaired.
senses.exampleCN: 除非并且直到屋顶修好，办公室才会重新开放。
senses.why: Two limiters side by side make the condition sound impossible to soften.
senses.whyCN: 两个限定词并排，让这个条件听起来无从通融。

intro.en: Unless is a worn-down phrase rather than a word built from parts: on less, meaning on a lesser condition.
intro.cn: unless 不是由词缀构成，而是一个磨短了的短语：on less，意为「在较小的条件下」。

items.en: The preposition on and the comparative lǣssa, less, stood side by side as on lǣssan, on a lesser condition.
items.cn: 介词 on 与比较级 lǣssa（较少）并列为 on lǣssan，意为「在较小的条件下」。

items.en: The phrase shrank to on lesse and then to unless, losing the space and then the o.
items.cn: 这个短语缩为 on lesse，再缩为 unless，先丢了空格，又丢了 o。

items.en: By the fourteenth century unless was used as a conjunction before a clause.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，unless 已用作引导从句的连词。

items.en: Lest, from a parallel phrase, kept the older meaning of avoiding something, and the two words divided the work.
items.cn: 由类似短语来的 lest 保留了「以免」的旧义，两个词于是各司其职。

items.en: Modern contracts fixed unless otherwise stated as a standard clause formula.
items.cn: 现代合同把 unless otherwise stated 固化为标准条款用语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers negatives and near forms in un- or less; the near-meaning group gathers conjunctions of condition that differ in strength.
note.cn: 形近组收以 un- 或 less 构成的否定词与近形词；近义组收表示条件的连词，力度不同。

entries.definition: Up to the time that; it names a moment, not a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「直到」，指时间点而非条件。

entries.definition: About, regarding; close in sound to the old prepositional use only.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「关于」。

entries.definition: For fear that; the older partner of unless.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「以免」，是 unless 较早的搭档词。

entries.definition: In spite of that; it contains less but means despite, not except.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「然而、不过」，含 less 但意为转折而非例外。

entries.definition: Nevertheless; it contains less but means in spite of that.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「尽管如此」，含 less 但意义不同。

entries.definition: The plain conditional with a negative; unless is its compressed form.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「如果不」，unless 是其压缩形式。

entries.definition: The full phrase behind unless, still used in careful speech.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「除非」，是 unless 的完整说法。

entries.definition: Only on the condition that; it states the condition positively.
entries.definitionCN: 连词短语，义为「只要」，从正面提出条件。

entries.definition: If not, or in other circumstances; often pairs with unless in clauses.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「否则」，常与 unless 在条款中配合使用。

entries.definition: As a precaution because something might happen; not the same as unless.
entries.definitionCN: 连词短语，义为「以防」，与 unless 不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the worn-down on less behind the word and the clauses it appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后磨短的 on less，以及它常出现的从句。

normal.en: Unless is on less in disguise: the one case on a lesser footing, the exception.
normal.cn: unless 是 on less 的变形：那个处于次要地位的唯一情形，就是例外。

normal.en: Unless you show your ticket, you cannot enter: the exception is the only open door.
normal.cn: unless you show your ticket 意为除非出示门票；例外就是唯一开着的门。

normal.en: Unless otherwise stated is the standard formula in contracts.
normal.cn: unless otherwise stated 是合同里的标准说法。

normal.en: Do not confuse unless with until: one is a condition, the other a time.
normal.cn: 不要把 unless 与 until 混用：一个是条件，一个是时间。

normal.en: Lest and unless once did the same work.
normal.cn: lest 与 unless 曾做同一份工作。

abstract.en: Picture a road with a single gate: unless is the gate, and nothing else lets you through.
abstract.cn: 想象一条只有一道门的路：unless 就是那道门，别的都通不过。

abstract.en: The word thinks in negatives: it names the only thing that can stop the statement from being true.
abstract.cn: 这个词用否定来思考：它指出唯一能让这句话不成立的事。

abstract.en: Every rule has a unless hidden in it, which is why contracts love the word.
abstract.cn: 每条规则里都藏着一个 unless，所以合同喜欢这个词。

examples.en: Do not call me unless it is urgent.
examples.cn: 除非有急事，否则别打电话给我。

examples.en: The meeting will go ahead unless the storm gets worse.
examples.cn: 除非暴风雨加剧，会议照常举行。

examples.en: Unless otherwise stated, all prices include tax.
examples.cn: 除非另有说明，所有价格均含税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的莱斯」——安说：除非莱斯先来，否则不开始：除非

root: 由中古英语短语 on lesse（在较小的条件下）缩合而成，源自 on 与比较级 lǣssa（较少）；十四世纪起作连词，与 lest 分工，现代又在合同里固定为 except 条件的标准说法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unless all name the one exception: the only case where the statement fails, whether spoken as a condition, a negative clause, an old preposition, a contract formula, or a doubled limiter.
sensesIntro.cn: unless 的五个义项都指那唯一的例外：这句话唯一不成立的情形，表现为条件、否定从句、古老介词、合同套语或叠用的限定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single open gate on an otherwise blocked road.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被挡住的路上一道唯一开着的门。

branches.en: THE EXCEPTION: the named case alone changes what happens.
branches.cn: 例外线：只有被点出的那种情形改变结果。

branches.en: THE NEGATIVE: after not, the exception becomes the only way in.
branches.cn: 否定线：在 not 之后，例外成了唯一的进路。

branches.en: THE OLD PREPOSITION: except for a thing, in older prose.
branches.cn: 旧介词线：在较早的书面语中表示「除某物之外」。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT: written rules need a word for the noted exception.
branches.cn: 合同线：书面规则需要一个词表示注明的例外。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE LIMIT: unless and until leaves no room to soften.
branches.cn: 双限线：unless and until 不给任何通融余地。

intro.en: This word has no affixes at all: it is a phrase worn down to six letters.
intro.cn: 这个词完全没有词缀：它是一个被磨短到六个字母的短语。

latinIntro.en: Nothing here is Latin; under this word sit the preposition on and an old comparative meaning less.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁成分；这个词底下是介词 on 与一个意为「较少」的古老比较级。

items.example: It survives only as the hidden first sound.
items.exampleCN: 它只作为隐藏的第一个音留存。

items.example: It is the modern shape of lǣssa.
items.exampleCN: 它是 lǣssa 的现代形式。

items.example: The comparative inside the old phrase.
items.exampleCN: 旧短语里的那个比较级。

items.example: A parallel contraction from þy læs þe.
items.exampleCN: 由 þy læs þe 并行的缩合词。

items.example: A look-alike that keeps less visible.
items.exampleCN: 一个把 less 留在表面的形近词。

items.example: The final form of on lesse.
Two limiters side by side in legal English.
items.exampleCN: 法律英语中并排使用的两个限定词。

definition_zh: 额外的；另外的；附加的（形容词）；额外的事物；临时演员（名词）；格外；特别（副词）
definition_en: more than what is usual or expected; added to the usual amount
core_image: 标准份之外的又一份：盘子边上多出来的那一小碟
scene: 旅店前台问要不要加床，爸爸看了看熟睡的孩子，点头说： We would like an extra blanket for the night.
sceneCN: 这里 extra 指「在标准之外另加的」（第 1 个义项：额外提供的）；句意为夜里需要再加一床毯子。

pos.zh: 额外的事物；另收费项目；临时演员

derivatives.zh: 非凡的；特别的（extra 加拉丁词根 ordinarius，义为「在常规秩序之外的」）
奢侈的；过度的（extra 加 vagari「游荡」，义为「游出边界之外的」）
外来的；无关的（同源正式词，义为「从外面进来的」）

senses.title: More than the usual amount
senses.definition: more of something than is usual, expected, or already provided
senses.definitionCN: 超出通常、预期或既定供给的量
senses.example: We would like an extra blanket for the night.
senses.exampleCN: 我们想夜里再加一床毯子。
senses.why: The Latin root means beyond or outside: the extra thing stands at the edge of the standard plate.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根义为「在…之外」：extra 的东西就站在标准盘子的边缘。

senses.title: Additional payment or charge
senses.definition: money charged beyond the normal price
senses.definitionCN: 超出正常价格的收费
senses.example: Breakfast at the hotel costs extra.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆的早餐要另外收费。
senses.why: The beyond-position turns to money: outside the fixed bill, one more sum waits.
senses.whyCN: 「之外」的位置换成了钱：固定账单之外还有一笔在等着。

senses.title: A person with no speaking part
senses.definition: a film or theatre performer without a speaking role
senses.definitionCN: 电影或戏剧中没有台词的表演者
senses.example: Hundreds of extras filled the battle scene.
senses.exampleCN: 数百名临时演员填满了战争场面。
senses.why: A person added beyond the needed cast: outside the story's main count, but visible on screen.
senses.whyCN: 超出必要班底而加上的人：不在主角计数之内，却在镜头里。

senses.title: Especially; very
senses.definition: used before an adjective to mean very or unusually
senses.definitionCN: 用在形容词前表示「非常」「格外」
senses.example: Be extra careful on the icy road.
senses.exampleCN: 结冰的路上要格外小心。
senses.why: The beyond-image intensifies: past the usual degree, one more step out.
senses.whyCN: 「之外」的意象转为强调：越过寻常程度，再往外一步。

intro.en: Extra is a Latin adverb meaning "beyond, outside", taken straight into English and grown into an adjective.
intro.cn: extra 是拉丁语副词「在…之外」，直接进入英语并长成形容词。

items.en: Latin extra meant "outside, beyond", used in phrases like extra muros, outside the walls.
items.cn: 拉丁语 extra 意为「在外面、超出」，用于 extra muros（城墙之外）等短语。

items.en: It is a cousin of exterus, "outward", which gave English external and exterior.
items.cn: 它是 exterus「向外的」的近亲，后者衍生出英语 external 与 exterior。

items.en: Eighteenth-century English borrowed it as an adjective, "added beyond the ordinary".
items.cn: 十八世纪英语把它借作形容词，义为「超出寻常之外而另加的」。

items.en: The noun followed in commerce: extras were items billed beyond the base price.
items.cn: 名词随之进入商业语：extras 指基本价之外的另计项目。

items.en: The adverb use as an intensifier and the film-extra sense completed the family.
items.cn: 作强调副词的用法与「临时演员」义补齐了这个词族。

note.en: These neighbours carry the same outside-the-line prefix or a related idea.
note.cn: 下列词带同样的「越界」前缀，或意思相近。

entries.definition: far beyond the ordinary
entries.definitionCN: 非凡的（extra + ordinary，常规之外）

entries.definition: spending beyond all limits
entries.definitionCN: 奢侈的（同前缀，游出边界）

entries.definition: on the outside
entries.definitionCN: 外部的（同 exterus 词根）

entries.definition: to draw out
entries.definitionCN: 提取；拔出（同前缀 ex-，义为「拉出来」）

entries.definition: added on
entries.definitionCN: 另外的；附加的（中性书面）

entries.definition: kept in reserve
entries.definitionCN: 备用的；多余的

entries.definition: amount left over beyond need
entries.definitionCN: 盈余；过剩（偏数量结果）

normalIntro.en: Five associations from the real root and usage.
normalIntro.cn: 五条来自真实词根与用法的联想。

normal.en: Extra in Latin simply means outside or beyond.
normal.cn: extra 在拉丁语里就是「外面、超出」。

normal.en: Extraordinary is the family star: beyond the ordinary.
normal.cn: extraordinary 是词族明星：超出寻常。

normal.en: Costs extra is the shop phrase for beyond the base price.
normal.cn: costs extra 是商店用语：基本价之外另算。

normal.en: Film extras are people added beyond the needed cast.
normal.cn: 电影里的 extra 是超出必要班底加上去的人。

normal.en: Extra large pushes size one step past large.
normal.cn: extra large 把尺码在 large 之上再推一步。

abstract.en: Picture a dinner plate: beside the standard serving sits one more small dish.
abstract.cn: 想象餐盘：标准份旁边又多了一小碟。

abstract.en: The edge of the standard is where everything extra lives.
abstract.cn: 所有 extra 都住在标准线的边缘。

abstract.en: Going beyond can be generous, costly, or simply off the wall.
abstract.cn: 「越出一步」可以是慷慨、昂贵，也可以是离谱。

examples.en: We would like an extra blanket for the night.
examples.cn: 我们想夜里再加一床毯子。

examples.en: Breakfast at the hotel costs extra.
examples.cn: 旅馆的早餐要另外收费。

examples.en: Be extra careful on the icy road.
examples.cn: 结冰的路上要格外小心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱克斯戳」——爱克斯（X）之外再戳一份，就是额外的。

root: 拉丁语副词 extra「在外面、超出」，与 exterus「向外的」（external、exterior）同族。十八世纪进入英语作形容词，随后派生名词、副词与「临时演员」义。

sensesIntro.en: From standing outside the standard, the word covers added amounts, added bills, added people, and added intensity.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「站在标准之外」出发，覆盖另加的量、另收的费、另加的人与格外强调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one more dish set at the edge of the standard plate
core.cn: 核心意象：标准盘边多出的一小碟

branches.en: beyond the usual measure or degree
branches.cn: 超出寻常的量或程度

branches.en: beyond the fixed bill
branches.cn: 固定账单之外的部分

branches.en: people beyond the needed cast
branches.cn: 必要班底之外的人

branches.en: added items share the outside position
branches.cn: 另加项同处「之外」位置

branches.en: the added ones stand at the frame's edge
branches.cn: 另加者站在画面边缘

intro.en: The family lives on the Latin ex- outside-line, stacking with other roots.
intro.cn: 词族生在拉丁 ex- 的「界外」义上，可与其他词根叠加。

latinIntro.en: Latin cousins keeping the beyond sense.
latinIntro.cn: 保留「超出」义的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 乐趣；享乐；有趣的人或事物
definition_en: enjoyment, amusement, or something that provides light-hearted pleasure
core_image: 孩子们在游乐场里大笑奔跑，笑声把空气都点亮了
scene: 游乐场的旋转木马转了起来，铃声和笑声混在一起。 The whole class agreed that the trip was great fun from start to finish.
sceneCN: 这里 fun 是「乐趣」（第 1 个义项：轻松愉快的体验）；句意为全班都说这次出行从头到尾都很有趣。

pos.zh: 乐趣；享乐；有趣的人或事
有趣的；令人愉快的（口语）

derivatives.zh: fun 加后缀 -ny 构成，义为「滑稽的；奇怪的」，语义从「有趣」偏移出「古怪」
复合词 fun + fair，义为「游乐场」

senses.title: Enjoyment or amusement
senses.definition: light-hearted pleasure, enjoyment, or good humour
senses.definitionCN: 轻松愉快的体验、消遣或好心情
senses.example: Swimming in the sea is pure fun for children.
senses.exampleCN: 在海里游泳对孩子们来说纯粹是乐趣。
senses.why: The word directly names the feeling of enjoyment, so this sense is the root of all others.
senses.whyCN: 这个词直接命名「愉悦」这种感受，因此它是其余义项的根。

senses.title: A source of amusement
senses.definition: a person, activity, or thing that causes enjoyment
senses.definitionCN: 带来快乐的人、活动或事物
senses.example: Our new teacher is real fun in every lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的新老师每堂课都特别有趣。
senses.why: What gives joy is labelled by the feeling itself, so the cause borrows the name of the effect.
senses.whyCN: 带来快乐的东西被用它产生的感受来称呼，于是「因」借用了「果」的名字。

senses.title: Playful, joking behaviour
senses.definition: playful joking, often teased at someone's expense
senses.definitionCN: 打趣、嬉闹的言行，常带调侃意味
senses.example: She said it all in fun, so nobody was hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 她完全是开玩笑说的，所以没人介意。
senses.why: Joking is enjoyment turned outward toward others, a playful branch of the amusement feeling.
senses.whyCN: 玩笑是把快乐转向他人的方式，是愉悦感的一个嬉闹分支。

senses.title: Amusing as an adjective
senses.titleCN: 有趣的；令人愉快的（形容词用法）
senses.definition: enjoyable and amusing, used informally before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 口语中放在名词前，表示令人愉快的
senses.example: They booked a fun weekend by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 他们预订了一个湖边的欢乐周末。
senses.why: English often turns popular nouns into adjectives, so fun slid into the describing slot.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把流行名词转作形容词，fun 由此滑入修饰语的位置。

senses.title: Light-hearted style or mood
senses.definition: an atmosphere of playful enjoyment at an event or place
senses.definitionCN: 活动或场所里充满嬉戏愉悦的气氛
senses.example: The fairground carried an air of fun all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 游乐场整个下午都洋溢着欢乐气氛。
senses.why: A place full of laughing people is sensed as a mood, so the feeling spreads over the setting.
senses.whyCN: 满是笑声的场所会被感受为一种氛围，于是感受弥散到整个场景。

intro.en: Fun is a short native word whose oldest recorded sense was trickery, not joy.
intro.cn: fun 是个简短的本土词，最早的书面含义是「欺骗」而非「快乐」。

items.en: Middle English fon and fonne meant a fool and to fool or trick someone.
items.cn: 中古英语 fon 与 fonne 指傻子，或动词「愚弄、欺骗」。

items.en: It is generally linked to Old French fon, fool, itself of uncertain deeper origin.
items.cn: 一般认为它与古法语 fon（傻子）相关，更早来源不确定。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the meaning shifted from trickery to playful amusement.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，词义从「捉弄」转为「嬉戏娱乐」。

items.en: The verb to fun and the adjective fun appeared as the noun spread.
items.cn: 名词流行后，动词 to fun 与形容词 fun 也出现了。

items.en: Modern English treats fun as noun, adjective, and the base of funny.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fun 用作名词、形容词，也是 funny 的基础。

note.en: Fun, funny, and fun sit close together and are easy to slip between.
note.cn: fun 与 funny、funny 的「古怪」义距离很近，容易混淆。

entries.definition: amusing or, confusingly, strange
entries.definitionCN: 滑稽的；（亦指）奇怪的；fun 的形容词派生，注意多义

entries.definition: an admirer, or a device for moving air
entries.definitionCN: 粉丝；风扇；拼写只差一个字母，词源无关

entries.definition: a joke using wordplay
entries.definitionCN: 双关语；拼写相近且同属玩笑话题，但词源不同

entries.definition: a strong feeling of happiness
entries.definitionCN: 欢乐；情绪强度高于 fun

entries.definition: the state of being entertained
entries.definitionCN: 娱乐；消遣，较正式的说法

entries.definition: the pleasure taken in something
entries.definitionCN: 享受；强调主观的愉悦体验

normalIntro.en: Five grounded hooks for fun.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于真实用法的 fun 记忆钩子。

normal.en: Make fun of means teasing, the old trickery sense still living inside.
normal.cn: make fun of 意为取笑，古老的「捉弄」义仍活在短语里。

normal.en: Funny adds -ny to fun but also gains a strange sense.
normal.cn: funny 由 fun 加 -ny 构成，但多出一个「古怪」义。

normal.en: For fun means just for play, no serious purpose.
normal.cn: for fun 表示纯粹闹着玩，没有严肃目的。

normal.en: Have fun is the farewell of every happy outing.
normal.cn: have fun 是每次愉快出游的告别语。

normal.en: A funfair is a fair full of fun, a compound you can hear.
normal.cn: funfair 就是充满 fun 的 fair，复合词读音自带提示。

abstract.en: Picture children running in circles, laughing for no reason at all.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子们绕圈奔跑，毫无缘由地大笑。

abstract.en: Hear the short bright sound of fun, like a quick laugh.
abstract.cn: fun 的发音短促明亮，像一声轻快的笑。

abstract.en: Fun once meant a trick; imagine a joke that turned into joy.
abstract.cn: fun 曾指捉弄，想象一个玩笑最终变成了快乐。

examples.en: We had a lot of fun at the beach.
examples.cn: 我们在海滩玩得很开心。

examples.en: Stop making fun of his haircut.
examples.cn: 别再取笑他的发型了。

examples.en: The quiz was fun and the whole class joined in.
examples.cn: 这次小测验很有趣，全班都参与了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「放」——把烦恼放开，就只剩下乐趣。

root: 一般认为来自中古英语 fon（愚弄、傻子），可能与古法语 fon（傻子）有关，更早来源不确定；词义从「捉弄」演变为「嬉乐」。

sensesIntro.en: The feeling of enjoyment is the root; sources of joy, jokes, adjective use, and atmosphere all branch from it.
sensesIntro.cn: 愉悦感受是根本；快乐的来源、玩笑、形容词用法与气氛都由此分支。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: laughter that lights up a moment
core.cn: 核心意象：点亮时刻的笑声

branches.en: the feeling and the mood it spreads
branches.cn: 感受及其弥散成的氛围

branches.en: people and things that cause joy
branches.cn: 带来快乐的人与事物

branches.en: teasing and joking
branches.cn: 调侃与玩笑

branches.en: fun as a describing word
branches.cn: 形容词化的 fun

branches.en: playfulness in words and acts
branches.cn: 言行中的嬉戏感

intro.en: Fun builds a compact family with suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: fun 用后缀与复合词构成一个小而紧凑的词族。

latinIntro.en: There are no Latin relatives: fun is a Germanic and French-tinged native word.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同源词：fun 是日耳曼本土词，仅与法语沾边。

items.example: A funny thing happened on the way.

items.meaning: the spot near the elbow that tingles when struck
items.meaningCN: 肘部麻筋；碰了会发麻的部位
items.example: He knocked his funny bone on the desk.
items.exampleCN: 他的肘部麻筋撞到了桌子。

items.example: A fun-loving crowd filled the park.
items.exampleCN: 一群爱玩乐的人挤满了公园。

items.example: They made fun of his accent.
She paints for fun, not for money.
items.exampleCN: 她画画只为乐趣，不为钱。

items.example: A sunnier, funnier script won the prize.
items.exampleCN: 更阳光更滑稽的剧本获奖了。

items.example: He is a big fan of the band.

definition_zh: 主题；题目；主旋律；（乐）主调；（店铺、派对等的）主题风格
definition_en: the main subject of a talk, book, or event; a recurring melody; or a style built around one idea
core_image: 一条主线从一堆素材里被抽出来：所有细节都挂在它上面
scene: 班会的横幅已经挂起来，孩子们在排练。 The theme of this year's science week is water.
sceneCN: 这里 theme 是「主题」（第 1 个义项：谈话或活动的中心题目）；句意：今年科学周的主题是水。

pos.zh: 主题；题目；主旋律；（语法）主题位

derivatives.zh: 主题的；主题相关的（theme 加形容词后缀构成）
按主题地；主题上（thematic 加副词后缀）
把……设为主题（学术用语）
主题公园（复合词）

senses.title: The main subject of a work or talk
senses.definition: the subject or idea that a talk, book, film or event keeps returning to
senses.definitionCN: 谈话、书籍、电影或活动反复回归的题目或思想
senses.example: Loneliness is the theme of her latest novel.
senses.exampleCN: 孤独是她新小说的主题。
senses.why: Out of many details one line is pulled straight: everything else hangs on it.
senses.whyCN: 从繁杂细节中抽直一条线：其余一切都挂在上面。

senses.title: A recurring melody in music
senses.definition: a short melody that returns and is developed throughout a piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 在乐曲中反复出现并被展开的短旋律
senses.example: The opening theme returns before the final movement.
senses.exampleCN: 开头的主题在末乐章前再次出现。
senses.why: A melody can do what an idea does: leave and come back, each time wearing new clothes.
senses.whyCN: 旋律能做思想做的事：离开又归来，每次都换上新衣。

senses.title: A style built around one idea
senses.definition: a style or setting arranged around a single idea, as in a themed party or park
senses.definitionCN: 围绕单一观念布置的风格或场景，如主题派对、主题公园
senses.example: The café opens with a railway theme.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆以铁路为主题开业。
senses.why: One idea becomes wallpaper, chairs and music: the theme leaves the page and furnishes the room.
senses.whyCN: 一个观念变成墙纸、座椅与音乐：主题离开纸面，开始布置房间。

senses.title: The starting point of a sentence in grammar
senses.definition: in linguistics, the point of departure of a sentence, what the sentence is about
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中句子的出发点，即句子所关涉者
senses.example: In this sentence, the weather stands as the theme.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个句子里，天气处于主题位。
senses.why: Grammar borrows the idea: a sentence also picks a line to hang its news on.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用此概念：句子也要挑一条线来挂自己的新信息。

intro.en: Theme goes back to Greek thema, a thing laid down or proposed, from tithenai, to place. The subject is literally the thing set down in front of the audience.
intro.cn: theme 可追溯到希腊语 thema「被放置、提出之物」，出自 tithenai「放置」。主题字面义就是摆在观众面前的那件东西。

items.en: Tithenai meant to place or set, and thema named what has been set down: a proposal, a subject.
items.cn: tithenai 意为放置；thema 指被放下之物：提案、题目。

items.en: The same placing root gave thesaurus, a treasure-house of laid-up words, and thesis, a thing set forth.
items.cn: 同一「放置」词根还给出 thesaurus「收藏语词的宝库」与 thesis「被摆出的论点」。

items.en: Latin borrowed thema and used it in rhetoric and music theory for the underlying subject.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 thema，用于修辞学与音乐理论中的底层题目。

items.en: English took theme through Latin texts, at first for the subject of a logical proposition.
items.cn: 英语经拉丁文本借得 theme，最初指逻辑命题的题目。

items.en: Modern English extended it to music, then to parties and parks styled around one idea.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到音乐，再扩展到围绕单一观念布置的派对与公园。

note.en: The first group walks the placing root into related words; the second separates theme from its near neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组沿「放置」词根走进相关词；第二组把 theme 与近邻分开。

entries.definition: a thing set forth; an argument placed before readers, from the same Greek placing root
entries.definitionCN: 论题；从同一希腊「放置」词根而来

entries.definition: the object pronoun; looks one letter from theme, unrelated in origin
entries.definitionCN: 宾格代词；字形只差一字母，词源无关

entries.definition: the adjective of theme, describing what belongs to the theme
entries.definitionCN: theme 的形容词，描述属于主题者

entries.definition: what is talked about; smaller and more concrete than theme
entries.definitionCN: 话题；比 theme 更小更具体

entries.definition: the area treated; subject names the field, theme names the idea inside it
entries.definitionCN: 题材；subject 指领域，theme 指其中思想

entries.definition: a recurring small pattern; a motif is a thread, a theme is the rope
entries.definitionCN: 反复出现的小图案；motif 是线，theme 是绳

normalIntro.en: Real links: the Greek placing root, the thesis of the same root, the theme song, and the themed café.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：希腊「放置」词根、同根的 thesis、主题曲、以及主题咖啡馆。

normal.en: Thema is a thing laid down: the subject placed before you.
normal.cn: thema 是被放下之物：摆在你面前的题目。

normal.en: Thesis and theme both come from placing something before readers.
normal.cn: thesis 与 theme 都来自「摆在读者面前」。

normal.en: A theme song returns like the idea it carries.
normal.cn: 主题曲像它承载的观念一样反复出现。

normal.en: Theme park: an idea big enough to furnish a whole park.
normal.cn: theme park：一个大到足以布置整座园子的观念。

normal.en: Motif is the thread; theme is the rope made of threads.
normal.cn: motif 是线；theme 是由线拧成的绳。

abstract.en: To have a theme is to choose what the rest must serve.
abstract.cn: 有了主题，就是选定其余一切必须服务的对象。

abstract.en: The strongest themes return quietly rather than loudly.
abstract.cn: 最有力的主题静默回归，而非喧哗。

abstract.en: An idea can decorate a room as easily as a paragraph.
abstract.cn: 观念布置房间与布置段落一样容易。

examples.en: The theme of the conference is cities and climate.
examples.cn: 本次大会的主题是城市与气候。

examples.en: The film's main theme returns at the closing scene.
examples.cn: 影片的主旋律在结尾场景再度响起。

examples.en: They decorated the hall on a harvest theme.
examples.cn: 他们以丰收为主题布置了大厅。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「西姆」——辩论赛抽到「西」「姆」两队对决，主题就定它了 → theme 主题

root: 希腊语 tithenai「放置」→ thema「被提出之物」→ 拉丁语 thema → 英语；同根词 thesis、thesaurus。

sensesIntro.en: From a thing set down before the audience, theme grows into the subject of works, the returning melody, the styled café or park, and even the grammarian's starting point.
sensesIntro.cn: 从摆在观众面前的物件出发，theme 长成作品题目、回归的旋律、有风格的咖啡馆与公园，乃至语法学家的出发点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one line pulled straight out of a heap of material, everything hanging on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一堆材料中抽直的一条线，万物挂其上。

branches.en: The placed thing becomes the subject.
branches.cn: 被放下之物成为题目。

branches.en: A melody repeats the placing: it returns and returns.
branches.cn: 旋律重复这一放置：反复回归。

branches.en: The idea leaves the page to furnish real rooms.
branches.cn: 观念离开纸面去布置真实房间。

branches.en: Grammar keeps the line for sentence openings.
branches.cn: 语法为句首保留这条线。

branches.en: Subject and melody share the shape of return.
branches.cn: 题目与旋律共享「回归」的形状。

intro.en: Theme builds the adjective thematic, the adverb thematically, and compounds with park and song.
intro.cn: theme 构成形容词 thematic、副词 thematically，并与 park、song 复合。

latinIntro.en: Latin thema is the channel from Greek; the placing root also produced thesis and thesaurus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 thema 是希腊词的通道；放置词根还造出 thesis 与 thesaurus。

items.example: The chapters follow a thematic order.

items.meaning: a statement set forth for argument
items.example: Her thesis defended a bold claim.
items.exampleCN: 她的论文为一个大胆论点辩护。

items.example: Use a thesaurus for richer wording.

items.meaning: a park built around one idea
items.example: The theme park opened in June.

items.meaning: the song linked to a show
items.example: The theme song topped the charts.

items.exampleCN: 该研究把都市孤独设为主题。

items.meaning: a map showing one chosen theme
items.example: A thematic map traced the rainfall.

definition_zh: 发展；开发；研制；成长
definition_en: to grow or change into a bigger, better or more complete form
core_image: 种子一天天长成小树的过程
scene: 学校的菜园里，我们种下番茄种子。 The little plants develop slowly in the warm spring sun.
sceneCN: 这里 develop 是「生长、成长」（第 1 个义项：逐渐长大变化）；句意是幼苗在温暖的春日下慢慢生长。

derivatives.zh: 由 develop 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「发展；开发」
由 develop 的现在分词转成形容词，义为「发展中的」
由 develop 加 -er 构成，义为「开发者；开发商」

senses.title: To grow into a fuller form
senses.definition: to grow or change gradually into a bigger or better state
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐长大或变为更好更完整的状态
senses.example: Her confidence developed after many school concerts.
senses.exampleCN: 经过多场校园演出，她的自信逐渐建立起来。
senses.why: Growth happens step by step, unseen between one day and the next.
senses.whyCN: 成长是一步步发生的，一天与一天之间悄然变化，这便是发展的本义。

senses.title: To create something new
senses.definition: to design and make something new or improve it
senses.definitionCN: 设计制造新事物或加以改进
senses.example: Scientists develop new ways to clean river water.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家开发净化河水的新方法。
senses.why: An idea also grows from a seed into a finished thing, so creation borrowed the growth word.
senses.whyCN: 想法也从种子长成成品，创造便借用了生长的词。

senses.title: To begin to have something
senses.definition: to start to have a habit, an interest or an illness
senses.definitionCN: 开始形成习惯、兴趣或出现疾病
senses.example: He developed a cough after the cold rainy trip.
senses.exampleCN: 那次寒冷多雨的行程之后他开始咳嗽。
senses.why: Habits and illnesses also grow quietly inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 习惯与疾病也在人身上悄然生长，所以「开始有」也用这个词。

intro.en: Develop comes from French words for unfolding.
intro.cn: develop 来自法语中表示「展开」的词。

items.en: Dis- plus volvere meant to unroll, to unwrap.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dis- 加 volvere 意为展开、解开。

items.en: French developed deweloper, to unwrap or unfold.
items.cn: 法语形成了 deweloper，意为展开、揭示。

items.en: English took develop in the seventeenth century, first for unfolding plans or images.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪吸收 develop，最初指展开计划或显影图像。

items.en: Photography used it for making pictures appear on film.
items.cn: 摄影术用它指使影像在底片上显现。

items.en: Industry and science widened it to growing ideas, skills and countries.
items.cn: 工业与科学把它扩展到想法、技能与国家的发展。

note.en: These words share the rolling root or describe growth.
note.cn: 这些词与「滚动」词根同源，或同样描述生长。

entries.definition: the act of growing or a new building area
entries.definitionCN: 发展；开发区

entries.definition: still growing
entries.definitionCN: 发展中的

entries.definition: to spin around
entries.definitionCN: 旋转（同根）

entries.definition: to roll in, to include
entries.definitionCN: 涉及（同根）

entries.definition: paper that wraps a letter
entries.definitionCN: 信封（同词源家族）

entries.definition: to become bigger
entries.definitionCN: 生长

entries.definition: to move forward
entries.definitionCN: 进步

entries.definition: to become better
entries.definitionCN: 改进

entries.definition: to spread out
entries.definitionCN: 扩张

entries.definition: to help something grow
entries.definitionCN: 培育

normalIntro.cn: 用「展开」的画面和 volv 词族记住 develop。

senses.title: To write letters
senses.definition: to write or say the letters of a word in the correct order
senses.definitionCN: 按正确顺序写出或说出单词的字母
senses.example: Can you spell your surname?
senses.exampleCN: 你能拼写你的姓吗？
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of letters in order.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示按顺序排列字母的含义。

senses.title: To say letters aloud
senses.definition: to say the letters of a word one by one
senses.definitionCN: 逐个说出单词的字母

senses.title: To mean trouble

definition_zh: 落下；滴落；掉下；放弃；下降；一滴；水珠
definition_en: to fall or let something fall, or a small round amount of liquid
core_image: 一颗水珠脱离叶尖，垂直落下
scene: 阳台的叶尖悬着雨珠，微风一过便散落花盆。 Rain dripped off the leaf, and each drop fell into the flowerpot below.
sceneCN: 这里 drop 是「落下、掉落」（第 1 个义项：因重力垂直下落）；句意：一滴雨珠从叶子上落进下面的花盆。

pos.zh: 落下；滴落；掉下；放弃；使下降

derivatives.zh: rain 加 drop 构成，义为「雨滴」
drop 加 out 构成，义为「辍学者；退出者」

senses.title: Fall downward
senses.definition: to fall, or to let something fall to the ground
senses.definitionCN: 下落，或让某物落向地面
senses.example: He dropped his keys on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 他在回家路上把钥匙弄掉了。
senses.why: The first image is a small thing leaving the hand and falling straight down.
senses.whyCN: 最初的意象是小物件脱手后径直落下。

senses.title: Fall as liquid
senses.definition: to fall in small round drops of liquid
senses.definitionCN: 以小颗液体形式落下
senses.example: Water dropped slowly from the leaking pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 水从漏水的管子里缓缓滴落。
senses.why: The falling thing narrows to one tiny round bead of water.
senses.whyCN: 下落之物缩小成一颗小小的圆水珠。

senses.title: Decrease in amount
senses.definition: to become lower in number, level, or price
senses.definitionCN: 数量、水平或价格变低
senses.example: The temperature dropped quickly after sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落后气温迅速下降。
senses.why: Falling through the air becomes falling on a chart or scale.
senses.whyCN: 空中的下落变成了图表或刻度上的下落。

senses.title: Give up or stop
senses.definition: to stop doing, planning, or mentioning something
senses.definitionCN: 停止做、计划或提及某事
senses.example: They decided to drop the old plan.
senses.exampleCN: 他们决定放弃旧计划。
senses.why: Letting a thing fall from the hand becomes letting it fall from attention.
senses.whyCN: 让东西从手上掉落，引申为让它从注意里掉落。

senses.title: A small amount of liquid
senses.definition: a small round amount of liquid
senses.definitionCN: 一小颗圆形液体
senses.example: There is not a drop of milk left in the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 杯子里一滴牛奶都不剩。
senses.why: The verb names the falling bead, then the bead itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词命名了坠落的水珠，进而命名水珠本身。

senses.title: A sudden fall in level
senses.definition: an amount or distance by which something goes down
senses.definitionCN: 某物下降的幅度或距离
senses.example: The plane felt a sudden drop of air.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机遭遇了一股突然的气流下降。
senses.why: The measured fall of price, level, or ground keeps the falling picture.
senses.whyCN: 价格、水平或地面的可测下降，仍保留下落的画面。

intro.en: Drop belongs to a small Germanic family about small falling beads of liquid.
intro.cn: drop 属于一个小小的日耳曼词族，核心是「坠落的小颗液体」。

items.en: Proto-Germanic *drupan meant to drip or fall in drops.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *drupan 意为滴落、成滴坠落。

items.en: Old English dropa named a small quantity of liquid; the verb meant to let fall in drops.
items.cn: 古英语 dropa 指少量液体；动词意为使其成滴落下。

items.en: Old Norse dropa influenced the English verb, strengthening the dropping sense.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 dropa 影响了英语动词形式，强化了「滴落」义。

items.en: Middle English extended the word to falling objects and falling numbers.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词扩展到坠物与数字的下降。

items.en: Modern English added giving up plans, dropping out, and dropping by.
items.cn: 现代英语又添了放弃计划、辍学、顺路拜访等用法。

note.en: These words stand near drop in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 drop 相邻。

definition_zh: 介绍；引进；引言；入门
definition_en: the act of making people known or bringing something in, or the opening part of a book or talk
core_image: 书的正文之前，有一页写着短短几段，把你领进门
scene: 新同事被带到办公区，组长领着他在每张桌前停下说一句。 The book's introduction explains why the author began.
sceneCN: 这里 introduction 是「引言、前言」（第 4 个义项：书或讲话的开头部分），句意为这本书的引言说明了作者为何动笔。画面里的物件：新同事、工位、书的扉页。

pos.zh: 名词：介绍；引进；引言；入门介绍

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「介绍；引进」
由 introduce 加 -ory 构成，义为「引导性的」
截短形式，义为「开场；引言」

senses.title: Making people known
senses.definition: the act of telling two people each other's names so that they can meet
senses.definitionCN: 说出两人名字使他们得以相识的行为
senses.example: A quiet introduction at the door saved them both embarrassment.
senses.exampleCN: 门口一句轻轻的介绍替两人都免了尴尬。
senses.why: The Latin action noun treats the handshake as a deed with a name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语的动作名词把这次握手当成一件有名字的事。

senses.title: Bringing something in
senses.definition: the act of putting a new thing, rule, or idea into use
senses.definitionCN: 把新事物、规定或想法投入使用的行为
senses.example: The introduction of the railway changed the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路的引进改变了整个山谷。
senses.why: The same leading-in image applies to machines and policies.
senses.whyCN: 「领进来」的图像同样用于机器与政策。

senses.title: A first course
senses.definition: a book or course that teaches the basics of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 讲解某学科基础知识的一本书或一门课
senses.example: This little grammar is a gentle introduction to Latin.
senses.exampleCN: 这本薄薄的语法书是拉丁语的温和入门。
senses.why: A beginner is led in, so the teaching material takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 初学者是被领进去的，于是入门教材也叫这个名字。

senses.title: The opening part
senses.definition: the first section of a book, speech, or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 书籍、演讲或乐曲的最初部分
senses.example: Read the introduction before you judge the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 先读引言，再评判论证。
senses.why: The opening leads the reader in, exactly what the Latin verb described.
senses.whyCN: 开头把读者领进去，正是那个拉丁动词所描述的。

intro.en: Introduction is the Latin noun on introducere, to lead someone in.
intro.cn: introduction 是建立在 introducere（把人领进来）上的拉丁语名词。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead; intro- meant inward.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导」，intro- 意为「向内」。

items.en: Introductio named the act of bringing someone or something in.
items.cn: introductio 指把人或物带进来的行为。

items.en: French kept the noun for a formal presentation of persons.
items.cn: 法语保留了这个名词，指对人的正式引见。

items.en: Printing gave it the sense of the opening pages of a book.
items.cn: 印刷术给了它「书的开篇」义。

items.en: Modern usage adds the introduction of machines and reforms.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上机器与改革的引进。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -duct- leading stem; the near-meaning group holds other opening words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -duct-「引导」词干；近义组收其他「开头」词。

entries.definition: The verb of leading someone in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「介绍；引进」。

entries.definition: The adjective for an opening section.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「引导性的」。

entries.definition: The making of goods or a show.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「生产；制作」，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A short note before the main text.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「序言」，作者自述写作缘由。

entries.definition: An opening note often written by someone else.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「前言」，多由他人撰写。

entries.definition: A general summary before the details.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「概述」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks treat the word as the doorway into a book or a group.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它当作一本书或一群人的门口。

normal.en: Introduce is the act; introduction is the act turned into a thing.
normal.cn: introduce 是动作，introduction 是被做成东西的动作。

normal.en: An introduction to economics leads you into the subject.
normal.cn: an introduction to economics 把你领进这门学科。

normal.en: Letters of introduction once opened doors in a new city.
normal.cn: 介绍信曾在陌生城市替你开门。

normal.en: The introduction of the railway is the same word used for machines.
normal.cn: the introduction of the railway 是同词用于机器。

normal.en: Skip the introduction and you may miss why the book exists.
normal.cn: 跳过引言可能就错过了这本书存在的理由。

abstract.en: An introduction is a corridor, not a room.
abstract.cn: 引言是走廊，不是房间。

abstract.en: Every introduction asks you to trust before you know.
abstract.cn: 每次介绍都在你了解之前先请你信任。

abstract.en: A good introduction hands you a lamp, not a map.
abstract.cn: 好的引言递给你一盏灯，而不是一张地图。

examples.en: His introduction to her was made by a mutual friend.
examples.cn: 他是通过一位共同的朋友认识她的。

examples.en: The introduction of parking fees angered local shops.
examples.cn: 停车费的引入让本地商铺不满。

examples.en: She wrote a short introduction to the second edition.
examples.cn: 她为第二版写了一篇简短的引言。

dict_mnemonic.text: intro（向内）+ duct（引导）+ ion——把人领进来的那段

root: 拉丁语 intro「向内」+ ducere「引导」→ introductio「引见」→ 古法语 → 英语 introduction。同族有 introduce、introductory、intro。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: making people known, bringing something new in, a beginner's course, and an opening section.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：让人相识、引进新事物、入门课程，以及开篇部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few short pages standing before the main text like a doorman.
core.cn: 核心意象：正文之前几页短文，像一个门房站在那里。

branches.en: THE HANDSHAKE: two people given each other's names.
branches.cn: 握手这条线：两个人被互相报出名字。

branches.en: THE RAILWAY: a new thing led into daily life.
branches.cn: 铁路这条线：新事物被领进日常生活。

branches.en: THE TEXTBOOK: a gentle first course.
branches.cn: 课本这条线：温和的第一课。

branches.en: THE PREFACE: the opening that explains the whole.
branches.cn: 序言这条线：解释全书的开头。

branches.en: THE LINK: both stand at a door and say what comes next.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都站在门口，说明接下来是什么。

intro.en: Introduction is intro- plus the root duct- "lead" and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: introduction 由 intro- 加词根 duct-「引导」与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin introductio and the participle introductus are recorded forms.

items.example: It marks the direction of entry.

items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 conduct 与 product。

items.example: The noun is the direct source.
The verb is the base of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的基础。
它构成 preface，意为先说在前。

items.example: It builds foreword, the word in front.

definition_zh: 分享；份额；股份；合用
definition_en: to give part of something to others, to use something together, a portion of something, or a unit of ownership in a company
core_image: 一块饼被切开，每人手里拿到相同的一角
scene: 她把蛋糕分给每个孩子。 She shared the cake with every child.

分享

senses.title: Give a part
senses.definition: to give part of something to other people
senses.definitionCN: 把某物的一部分给别人
senses.example: She shared the cake with every child.
senses.exampleCN: 她把蛋糕分给每个孩子。
senses.why: This is the everyday social sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常社交义项。

senses.title: Use together
senses.definition: to use something with another person
senses.definitionCN: 与他人一起使用某物
senses.example: They share a small office.
senses.exampleCN: 他们合用一间小办公室。
senses.why: Sharing can mean joint use rather than division.
senses.whyCN: 分享也可以指共同使用而非分割。

senses.title: Portion
senses.definition: a part of something that belongs to one person
senses.definitionCN: 某物中属于某个人的部分
senses.example: Everyone got a fair share.
senses.exampleCN: 每个人都得到公平的一份。
senses.why: The act of dividing produces shares.
senses.whyCN: 分割的行为产生了份额。

senses.title: Company stock
senses.definition: one of the equal parts of a company's ownership
senses.definitionCN: 公司所有权中均等的一份
senses.example: He bought shares in the company.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了这家公司的股份。
senses.why: Ownership is divided into shares like a cake.
senses.whyCN: 所有权像蛋糕一样被分成份额。

definition_zh: 波浪；挥手；波（声、光、电磁等）；浪潮；（情绪的）一阵；使成波浪形
definition_en: a ridge of water moving across a surface; also a hand gesture, a physical oscillation, and a surge of events or feeling
core_image: 海面上一道隆起的水脊向前推，到了岸边翻卷、散成白沫
scene: 退潮后的沙滩上，孩子追着一道涌上来的水脊跑，脚背被拍了一下，他说， A wave broke over my feet and pulled the sand from under them.
sceneCN: 这里 wave 指「水面向前推进的隆起水脊」（第 1 个义项：海上的波浪）；句意为：一道浪打过我的脚背，把脚下的沙也抽走了。

pos.zh: 波浪；波（物理）；挥手；浪潮；一阵（情绪）
挥手示意；飘动；使成波浪形

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成：波浪形的；起伏的
由前一形容词加性质名词后缀构成：起伏不平的状态
由本词加表示「长度」的成分构成：波长，两个波峰之间的距离
由本词加表示「形状」的成分构成：波形，信号起伏画出的形状
由表示「微小」的前缀加本词构成：微波；用微波炉加热
由本词加指小后缀构成：小波；信号分析中的小波

senses.title: A ridge on the water
senses.definition: a raised ridge of water travelling across the surface of the sea or a lake, often breaking when it reaches shallow water
senses.definitionCN: 在海面或湖面上向前推进的隆起水脊，到浅水处常会翻卷破碎
senses.example: A wave broke over my feet and pulled the sand from under them.
senses.exampleCN: 一道浪打过我的脚背，把脚下的沙也抽走了。
senses.why: the noun came from Old English wǣg 'billow', the name of a moving ridge of water; this is the literal core that every other sense borrows from.
senses.whyCN: 名词出自古英语 wǣg「巨浪」，本义就是水中移动的脊；这是其余所有义项借用的字面核心。

senses.title: A sign with the hand
senses.definition: a movement of the hand held up and moved from side to side, used to greet, signal or say goodbye
senses.definitionCN: 举起手左右摆动，用来打招呼、示意或告别
senses.example: She gave a quick wave from the platform and disappeared into the train.
senses.exampleCN: 她在站台上匆匆挥了一下手，就消失在车厢里。
senses.why: the noun form of this sense grew from the verb: a single act of moving the hand to and fro was turned into a countable event.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项的名词形式是从动词长出来的：把一次来回动手的动作，变成了一个可数的事件。

senses.title: A physical oscillation
senses.definition: a disturbance that transfers energy through a medium or through space, repeating in time and distance
senses.definitionCN: 在介质或空间中传递能量的扰动，在时间与距离上重复出现
senses.example: Sound travels as a wave that compresses the air in front of it.
senses.exampleCN: 声音以波的形式传播，压缩前方的空气。
senses.why: physics took the water picture and generalised it: anything that repeats through space and time is drawn with the same rising and falling shape.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把水的图像一般化：任何在空间与时间上重复的东西，都用同一种起伏形状来画。

senses.title: A sudden surge of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden rise and passing of a feeling that affects a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 突然涌起又退去、影响一个人或一群人的情感
senses.example: A wave of relief passed through the ward when the doctor smiled.
senses.exampleCN: 医生一笑，一阵宽慰的波浪掠过病房。
senses.why: a feeling that comes in cycles and then passes behaves like water, so English counts emotions in waves rather than in units.
senses.whyCN: 情绪一波波涌来又退去，行为像水，因此英语用「波」来计数情感，而不是用单个单位。

senses.title: A wave of events
senses.definition: a cluster of similar events arriving close together, as in a crime wave or a wave of protests
senses.definitionCN: 同类事件集中在一段时间内接连发生，如犯罪浪潮或抗议浪潮
senses.example: The city reported a wave of bicycle thefts last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市去年春天报告了一波自行车失窃案。
senses.why: statistics describe clustered events as arriving in successive crests, so a rise in the count is drawn as a wave even when no water is involved.
senses.whyCN: 统计把集中发生的事件说成一个个接连而来的波峰，因此计数上升时，即便没有水，也画成一道浪。

senses.title: A curve in the hair
senses.definition: a curl or series of curves pressed or set into hair
senses.definitionCN: 在头发上做出的卷曲或一连串弧形
senses.example: A single wave in her hair softened the whole portrait.
senses.exampleCN: 她头发上的一道波浪让整幅肖像柔和下来。
senses.why: a lock of hair bent into alternating curves reproduces a water wave in miniature, so hairdressing kept the noun for the shape.
senses.whyCN: 一缕头发弯成交替的弧线，就是水波的缩小版，因此美发业保留了这个名词来指那种形状。

senses.title: A drawn line on an instrument
senses.definition: one rise and fall traced by a signal on a graph, screen or recording
senses.definitionCN: 信号在图表、屏幕或记录上画出的一次起伏
senses.example: The oscilloscope drew a clean wave across the screen.
senses.exampleCN: 示波器在屏幕上画出一道干净的波形。
senses.why: an instrument traces rising and falling voltage as a line, and the drawn shape is literally called a wave, so the graph keeps the sea's name.
senses.whyCN: 仪器把升降的电压画成一条线，画出的形状就被直接叫作波，图表于是沿用了海的名字。

senses.title: To move the hand
senses.definition: to move the hand or an object held in it to and fro, usually as a greeting or signal
senses.definitionCN: 把手或手中的东西来回挥动，通常表示招呼或示意
senses.example: He waved until the car turned the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直挥手，直到汽车转过街角。
senses.why: the verb sense keeps the older gesture meaning, from Old English wafian 'to move to and fro', which is a different source from the noun.
senses.whyCN: 动词义保留较古的手势义，出自古英语 wafian「来回挥动」，与名词的来源并不相同。

senses.title: To set into curves, or flutter
senses.definition: to give hair a wavy shape, or of a flag, cloth or branch, to move in curves in the wind
senses.definitionCN: 把头发做成波浪形；或指旗、布、枝条在风中起伏摆动
senses.example: Flags waved along the pier as the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风起时，码头上的旗子一路飘动。
senses.why: the same verb extends from the hand to anything made to move in curves, from hair set in waves to cloth lifting in the wind.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词从手扩展到任何被弄成曲线运动的东西，从做成波浪的头发到风中掀起的布。

intro.en: Wave has two Old English sources: the noun wǣg 'billow' and the verb wafian 'to move to and fro'. They are generally treated as separate formations that came to share one spelling in Middle English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: wave 有两个古英语来源：名词 wǣg「巨浪」与动词 wafian「来回挥动」。学界一般把它们视为两个不同的构造，到中古英语才共用同一个拼写。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wǣg meant a moving ridge of water, 'billow, surge'; it is the noun that survives in modern wave and still names the sea's ridge.
items.cn: wǣg 指水中移动的脊，即「巨浪、涌浪」；它就是留存到现代 wave 的名词，仍指海上的水脊。

items.en: The Germanic noun is reconstructed as *wēgaz; it is generally connected with a root meaning 'to carry, move', though that link is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 其日耳曼名词重构为 *wēgaz；一般认为它与表示「运送、移动」的词根有关，但这一联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Wafian meant 'to move the hand or an object to and fro'; it is a separate verb, not a derivative of the noun wǣg.
items.cn: wafian 意为「把手或物件来回挥动」；它是一个独立的动词，并非名词 wǣg 的派生。

items.en: Both words came to be spelled wave, and the noun widened from a water ridge to a mass of advancing troops, events or feeling.
items.cn: 两个词都写成 wave，名词也从水脊扩展到推进的人群、事件或情感。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century physics began drawing waves on paper, and the vocabulary of wavelength, waveform and wave theory followed.
items.cn: 18 与 19 世纪的物理学开始在纸上画波，wavelength、waveform 与波理论等词汇随之出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (root relation, not first date): whether wǣg and wafian descend from a single root is disputed, and they are usually described as two formations that merged in spelling; the date of the first figurative wave of is approximate, and *wēgaz is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指词根关系，不是首见年代）：wǣg 与 wafian 是否同出一根有争议，通常被描述为两个构造在拼写上合并；最早的比喻搭配（「一波……」这类说法）年代只是约数，*wēgaz 属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the derived forms of wave and one sound-alike with a different root; group two holds the sea words that differ in size, shape or behaviour.
note.cn: 第一组是 wave 的派生形式，以及一个词根不同的同音形近词；第二组是规模、形状或行为不同的海面用词。

entries.definition: from Old French weyver 'to abandon', probably of Scandinavian origin; it sounds identical to wave but means to give up a right, fee or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 weyver「放弃」，源头可能在斯堪的纳维亚语；它与 wave 同音，却意为放弃权利、费用或规则。

entries.definition: wave plus -y: having a shape that rises and falls in curves, used of hair, lines and edges.
entries.definitionCN: wave 加 -y：形状呈起伏的曲线，多用于头发、线条与边缘。

entries.definition: the distance between two successive crests; it is a measurement, not an object you can see on the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 相邻两个波峰之间的距离；它是一个量值，不是海上看得见的物体。

entries.definition: wave plus -let 'small': a small wave, and in modern signal analysis a short, localised wave shape.
entries.definitionCN: wave 加指小后缀 -let：小浪；在现代信号分析中指短而局部化的波形。

entries.definition: a long regular rise of the sea, often from distant weather, that has not yet steepened or broken.
entries.definitionCN: 海面上长而规则的起伏，常来自远处的天气，尚未变陡或破碎。

entries.definition: a very small wave on a surface, usually made by a light wind or a thrown stone.
entries.definitionCN: 水面极小的波，通常由微风或投石造成。

entries.definition: a wave that has begun to curl and fall as it reaches shallow water or a reef.
entries.definitionCN: 到达浅水或礁石时开始卷起、崩落的浪。

entries.definition: a great rolling mass of water, cloud or smoke; it stresses volume and movement rather than a single crest.
entries.definitionCN: 水、云或烟的一大团翻滚体；它强调体积与运动，而非单个波峰。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The noun is Old English wǣg 'billow'; the verb is wafian 'move the hand' — two sources, one spelling.
normal.cn: 名词是古英语 wǣg「巨浪」，动词是 wafian「挥动手」——两个来源，一个拼写。

normal.en: The family runs wave, wavy, waviness, wavelength, waveform, microwave, wavelet.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 wave、wavy、waviness、wavelength、waveform、microwave、wavelet。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physics: sound wave, shock wave, light wave, wave height.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：声波、冲击波、光波、波高。

normal.en: Figurative waves are counted: a wave of relief, a crime wave, a wave of protests.
normal.cn: 比喻的波可以计数：一阵宽慰、一波犯罪、一波抗议。

normal.en: One word covers hand and water because both go up and down and come back again.
normal.cn: 一个词同时覆盖手与水，因为两者都是上下往复。

abstract.en: Picture a single crest that keeps its shape while the water inside it stays almost in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一道波峰保持形状往前，而构成它的水几乎停在原处。

abstract.en: Picture a hand and a swell making the same arc in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手与一道涌浪在空中画出同一条弧。

abstract.en: Picture a microphone drawing a line that rises and falls like water.
abstract.cn: 想象一支麦克风画出一条像水一样起伏的线。

examples.en: The buoy recorded a wave nearly twelve metres high.
examples.cn: 浮标记录到一道近十二米高的浪。

examples.en: She waved from the window until the bus was out of sight.
examples.cn: 她在窗前挥手，直到公交车看不见为止。

examples.en: A wave of new students filled the lecture hall in September.
examples.cn: 九月，一波新生坐满了讲堂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挥」——挥手是 wave，海浪一来一回也像在挥手 → 波浪、挥手、波动

root: 名词古英语 wǣg「浪、波涛」（日耳曼语重构 *wēgaz，一般认为是印欧「运送、移动」词根的派生）；动词古英语 wafian「来回挥动」；两源在中古英语合为 wave，现代义由水浪扩展到挥手、物理波与「浪潮」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses split between two old sources: the sea's ridge and its physical descendants, then the hand's gesture and everything else that moves to and fro in curves, with the counted surge of feeling and events in between.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分属两个古老来源：先是由海浪扩展出的物理义，再是手势以及一切来回成曲线运动的东西，中间夹着可计数的情感与事件涌动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ridge of water moving forward while the water itself only rises and falls in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道水脊向前推进，而构成它的水只是原地上下起伏。

branches.en: THE DRAWN SHAPE: the sea's ridge and the oscilloscope's curve are one geometry seen twice.
branches.cn: 被画出的形状：海上的水脊与示波器上的曲线，是同一种几何看了两遍。

branches.en: THE HAND: the noun of greeting and the verb of greeting are the same gesture in two grammatical shapes.
branches.cn: 手：招呼的名词与动词，是同一个手势的两种语法形态。

branches.en: THE GENERALISED MOTION: physics extends the ridge to sound and light, and the verb to flags and hair.
branches.cn: 被推广的运动：物理学把水脊扩展到声与光，动词则扩展到旗与头发。

branches.en: SURGES COUNTED: feelings pass in crests, and social statistics cluster in waves.
branches.cn: 可计数的涌动：情感一波波过去，社会统计也一波波聚集。

branches.en: THE SHAPE IN HAIR: a curl repeats the water curve in miniature.
branches.cn: 头发里的形状：一道卷发把水的曲线缩小重演。

intro.en: Wave is a native Germanic word; its family grows by suffixes and compounds, and the same shape-word serves physics, hairdressing and signal analysis.
intro.cn: wave 是日耳曼本族词；它的词族靠后缀与复合扩展，同一个「形状词」同时服务物理学、美发与信号分析。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no cognate for wave: its word for a wave was unda, which gives English undulate but is unrelated to wave. That is why the Latin entries stay empty, and only the borrowed suffix -al appears elsewhere in the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有 wave 的同族词：它表示波浪的词是 unda，由此产生的英语词与 wave 并无亲缘。因此拉丁条目留空；词族里唯一的外来成分是别处出现的后缀 -al。

items.example: Old English wǣg named the billow that breaks on the shore.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 wǣg 指拍碎在岸上的巨浪。

items.structure: Old English wafian (verb, 'to move to and fro')
items.example: Old English wafian meant to move the hand to and fro.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 wafian 意为把手来回挥动。

items.meaning: a sea wave; to move the hand
items.example: Wave your hand when the boat comes.
The wavy edge follows the old shoreline.
items.exampleCN: 那条波浪形的边缘沿着旧岸线走。

items.example: The waviness of the glass distorts the horizon.
items.exampleCN: 玻璃的起伏把地平线弄歪了。

items.example: Red light has a longer wavelength than blue.
The waveform flattened after the filter.
Microwave links carry the signal inland.
items.exampleCN: 微波链路把信号送向内陆。

items.meaning: a small wave; a short localised waveform
items.example: A wavelet crossed the quiet harbour.
items.exampleCN: 一道小浪掠过平静的港湾。
